## 1. Outcome and scope

The first delivery target is a complete external REST workflow. A client can retrieve an approved engineering configuration and operating target, submit a measurement, retrieve qualified evidence, calculate a reproducible deviation, and record an authorized operator response. Every accepted step produces a durable result that another client can retrieve after an application restart.

Start with **scoped Planning authoring and independent approval**. It closes the first business decision loop and creates the authoritative target used by Monitoring. Build engineering baseline release and trusted Telemetry as distinct prerequisites for the integrated workflow. After the first integrated proof, complete the remaining business lifecycles and add non-numerical scenario readiness.

This plan derives its scope and acceptance criteria from the [HidraAPI Functional API and Workflow Assessment](https://chatgpt.com/library?file_id=libfile_9aacabc70b488191a51c695c8b0b1045&account_id=personal). The assessment inspected 24 modules, 387 REST operations and 13 workflows at [HidraAPI commit 85ac6d3](https://github.com/CHOUABBIA-AMINE/HidraAPI/commit/85ac6d387ef5cf1421dd22a89b9c56079d665e1e). The sequence, scope boundaries and proposed acceptance gates below are defined within this document. Identifiers beginning with **FG** and **A** refer only to the assessment’s findings and acceptance cases.

**Delivery boundary.** This is a proposed backend plan for software qualification with synthetic fixtures. The first integrated result includes a reproducible operator decision. Numerical execution, field calibration, real SCADA/OT integration, deployment, SITE acceptance and autonomous control remain outside its delivery scope. The future Hidra-owned steady and transient engine uses the versioned inputs established here.

## 2. Starting point

| Capability | Reuse from assessed source | Remaining work |
|---|---|---|
| Native API foundation | Signed LOCAL access, current authorization patterns, Organization and Party reference data, typed Configuration, selected Workflow actions, native PostgreSQL/JVM evidence for bounded journeys. | Apply exact scope and actor authority to each new owner transition and query. |
| Engineering | Existing network, station, equipment, product and manufacturer operations. Combined baseline draft and validation. | Scoped discovery, independent approval of the exact combined baseline, publication and effective/historical reads. |
| Planning | Period and plan creation, typed reads, revision metadata concurrency and approval actions for already linked instances. | Company-owned periods, scope-aware reads/counts, client-authored revisions and targets, atomic submission, independent decision and final readback. |
| Telemetry and Monitoring | Native raw ingestion, replay and readback. Rule registration and supplied deviation intake. | Commissioned bindings, trusted publication, rule activation and authoritative evaluation from approved and qualified inputs. |
| Operational response | Manual alarms and authorized handling. Selected leak, incident and HSE operations. | Correlation from qualified evidence, deduplication, escalation and typed owner outcomes. |
| Broader API | Partial create/read/lifecycle paths across remaining business modules. | Complete workflow-specific commands, results, histories and typed queries where the assessment identified gaps. |

The assessed local checks passed ten focused API tests and eleven frontend adapter tests, and the frontend build passed. The latest-pair native HTTP/PostgreSQL workflow was unverified. Completion gates below require new end-to-end evidence for the selected API delivery.

## 3. Delivery sequence

The table defines the proposed order of delivery. A row can start once its own prerequisites are satisfied. Planning does not require an ingested measurement to create a target. Monitoring joins the approved target with a trusted observation. The engineering release is required for envelope-based evaluation and for the integrated GZ2 workflow.

| Increment | Deliverable | Entry dependencies | Exit evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. Planning (T01–T03) | Company-owned period → asset-scoped plan → versioned revision and target → independent Workflow decision → authorized readback. | Current company and resource authorization, effective responsibility, eligible asset and point/unit references, and an active Workflow definition for the exact revision. | Signed REST over PostgreSQL proves approve and reject, scoped counts, CAS, atomic rollback and restart readback. A03 and the Planning slice of A18. FG-03 and FG-18. |
| 2. Engineering release (T04–T07) | Discover exact eligible inputs → complete baseline draft → independent approval → publication → current/as-of/history. | Published network, station, installed equipment, manufacturer and product revisions for the supported GZ2 fixture. | The published manifest retains exact input IDs and digest. Supersession preserves history. Stale or withdrawn sources and unauthorized publication are rejected. A01/A02. FG-01 and FG-02. |
| 3. Trusted Telemetry (T08–T09) | Commission a source, point and effective binding → ingest → assess → publish and retrieve trusted evidence. | Current source principal, exact asset association, unit/quality policy and a valid effective binding. | Correct raw replay, one qualified result where eligible, traceable evidence and explicit stale, rejected and mismatched cases. A04. FG-04. |
| 4. Monitoring evaluation (T10–T11) | Activate a versioned rule → evaluate authoritative inputs → persist result and deviation → explain it through REST. | Accepted outputs from 1 and 3. Output from 2 when the rule uses engineering limits or baseline context. | Deterministic actual/expected/difference and exact evidence references. Explicit result for stale, missing, uncertain and incompatible observations. A05. FG-05. |
| 5. Operational response (T12–T14) | Raise a correlated alarm or suspected leak → acknowledge → escalate through authorized human action → retrieve owner outcome. | Scoped evaluation or other explicitly eligible evidence from 4, plus an admitted trigger, deduplication and escalation policy. | Replayed evidence does not duplicate the outcome. Human decision, case link and timeline remain retrievable. A06 and the escalation slice of A07. FG-06 and the escalation slice of FG-07. |
| 6. Integrated GZ2 software acceptance (T15) | Run the complete engineering-to-operator journey on one exact API commit with an independent client. | Required outputs from 1–5 are accepted and compatible. | Fresh PostgreSQL and signed HTTP proof with actual generated OpenAPI, persisted readback, negative cases and independently reviewed evidence. |
| 7. Remaining business lifecycles (T16–T30) | Complete investigations, maintenance, Custody, Risk, Analytics, Reporting, Documents, Integration, Notification and Audit. | Exact owner prerequisites for each workflow. Documents capability is available before report artifact completion depends on it. | Each selected workflow can be initiated, progressed, completed and retrieved through authorized REST. FG-07–18. |
| 8. Scenario readiness and configuration (T31–T32) | Add engine-neutral scenario versioning and reconstruction. Deliver historical configuration retirement only for a proven consumer need. | Accepted engineering inputs and a defined capability/validation policy. | Historical scenario reconstructs after supersession. Configuration lookup remains reproducible. FG-19 and FG-20. FG-21 remains deferred. |
| 9. Circle 1 regional workplace (T33–T39) | Regional authorized GZ2 pipeline, dossier, constraints, telemetry and governed decisions. | Completed regional authority and owner-supported input contracts. | Exact-SHA signed HTTP and PostgreSQL consumer handoff (already recorded). |
| 10. Circle 1 release alignment (T40) | Maven 0.7.0 candidate, release and audit governance. | T39 accepted and separately governed release publication. | Exact-SHA CI/audit evidence, with unresolved already-published tag/release reconciliation explicitly retained. |
| 11. Circle 2 supporting references (T41–T58) | Secure Party, Configuration and Documents reference workplace joined to the Circle 1 GZ2 asset context. | C1 owner contracts, admitted policy and protected authority in T41, and prerequisites of the nine active C2 packages; SKIPPED IDs require no separate execution. | Authorized end-to-end manufacturer, effective non-secret configuration and controlled-document version/byte evidence; independently verified API and browser handoff. |

Increment 6 is the proposed first integrated development milestone. The remainder is sequenced by functional dependency and risk. Calendar estimates require implementation sizing, staffing and CI feedback.

## 4. Explicit delivery task register

The roadmap initially contained **32 registered tasks**; T33–T40 added Circle 1 and release work. All C2 IDs T41–T58 remain tracked (58 total IDs), with nine active PLANNED C2 packages and nine SKIPPED consolidated-only planning rows. SKIPPED is not implemented or accepted work. Use these IDs for HidraAPI task selection and evidence. Each task delivers a named API capability or a verifiable acceptance result. An owner is the accountable bounded context, with collaborators shown where needed. Dependencies are prerequisites for accepting the result and take precedence over task numbering. “Existing foundation” means the assessed starting capabilities in §2.

A task includes its required authorization, REST contract, persistence, failure handling and tests. Confirm exact routes, payloads and errors during task preparation. Each task inherits the definition of done in §7.

T41–T58 were registered as eighteen PLANNED items on 2026-11-22.
The owner then approved reworking the overly granular scope into
**nine coherent Circle 2 packages**. The nine active PLANNED task IDs are
T41, T43, T44, T46, T48, T50, T52, T55 and T56. The other nine IDs

independent planned delivery packages**, with their original requirements
transferred to surviving tasks, not completed or waived. T01–T58 task
numbering and the original C2-01–C2-18 mapping remain traceable.
The original eighteen task rows are retained verbatim in a fenced historical

**C2 security and acceptance invariants.** Server-side Identity grants and
denies, company and resource scope, current regional authority, authorization
before protected list/count/history/bytes, independent decisions where
admitted, optimistic concurrency, exact revision/effective times, verified
file length/checksum, immutable historical evidence and owner-only aggregate
mutations are mandatory. Configuration environment and module owner metadata
do not imply company or industrial-resource authority. Feature flags grant no
permissions and activate neither OT control nor an absent engine. A controlled
Document acceptance is not an approval of pressure limits or other engineering
facts. Use signed HTTP, fresh PostgreSQL/Flyway and synthetic fixtures; skipped
database tests do not establish persistence acceptance. C2 backend acceptance
does not establish HidraWEB browser, industrial calibration, SITE, live SCADA,
production or numerical simulation acceptance.

**Policy gates:** T41 records Party consumer visibility, Configuration
allowlisted non-secret context, admitted Documents target classes,
classification/acceptance responsibility and a non-destructive retention/
evidence-hold default. T43/T46/T50/T55 may not invent missing resource,
authorization or retention policy. T55 does **not** authorize purge,
automatic deletion or industrial retention durations. Such behavior
requires a separate approved policy and future registered task.
Unresolved calibration values do not block secure configurable contracts
tested on synthetic inputs.

**Decision dependencies.** Before T33 selection, record whether an effective
Organization responsibility constrains Identity grants or can contribute
access through an explicitly approved policy, and define cross-region
geometry and metadata disclosure. Regional membership and employee title
alone confer no access. Before T36 or T38 selection, identify the owning
engineering authority for each admitted constraint class and its approved
source and decision rules.

in parallel after regional authority is settled. The read-only milestone
includes authorized decision references and readback where an authoritative
source supplies them. Full Circle 1 adds the governed restriction decision
path in T38. T39 is the API consumer handoff and integration proof. The
matching integration and browser acceptance remain governed by HidraWEB.
Use synthetic, gas-first GZ2 fixtures for software acceptance. Site
qualification, live OT integration and numerical solver work retain their
separate gates.

## 5. Detailed delivery specifications

### 1. Scoped Planning and independent approval

**Business result.** An authorized author starts from eligible reference data and obtains an immutable, independently approved target. Monitoring can retrieve its exact effective value, unit, time window and revision.

| Delivery area | Required behavior | Proof |
|---|---|---|
| Period and plan | Each period has one authoritative company. Resolve the authenticated actor and current company grant server-side. Validate the plan’s exact asset/company binding and organizational responsibility. Carry ownership through descendants. | Two synthetic companies. A period and plan created through REST remain visible only to entitled principals. Same-company access to asset A does not imply access to asset B. |
| Revision and targets | Generate revision IDs, sequence and version tokens server-side. Allow editing only in an eligible draft. Check target type, engineering unit, point/asset binding and effective window. Freeze submitted targets and retain previous approved revisions. | Bad unit, wrong binding, stale version and concurrent writers yield deterministic outcomes. Old approved evidence remains reconstructible after a newer revision. |
| Submission and review | Bind the active Workflow definition to the exact revision. Persist submission, immutable target snapshot and Workflow link in the same PostgreSQL transaction. Recheck independent reviewer authority at decision time. Activate a target only on committed approval. | Force a downstream error and verify no orphan instance or partial Planning state. Exercise self-review denial, revoke, reject, repeat transition and two simultaneous submissions. |
| Read and counts | Provide typed period/plan/revision/target/approval responses. Filter authorized rows in the database before pagination and count. Keep foreign and missing cases non-disclosing. | Compare list, detail, counts and approval access for author, reviewer, unrelated asset and revoked principal. Verify authorized reads from a restarted JVM. |
| REST and storage | Retain accepted APIs where compatible. Add explicit authoring and submission commands, typed DTOs, statuses, version fields and deterministic problem responses. Inspect current global period-code uniqueness and specify the correct uniqueness scope before any forward-only DDL. | Fresh PostgreSQL migration and JPA proof. Existing metadata CAS and error contract pass regressions. Runtime OpenAPI documents the added client journey. |

Planning owns periods, plans, revisions and targets. Workflow owns tasks and decisions. Identity, Organization, Topology and Telemetry provide their respective owner contracts. The initial deliverable includes the full target approval journey. **Nomination authoring is an extension** of the Planning workflow and receives its own acceptance in increment 7. This preserves a coherent first result without making the downstream Monitoring calculation depend on nomination lifecycle work.

### 2. Approved engineering configuration

1. Provide typed, scope-aware discovery by business key for eligible network, station, installed equipment, product and manufacturer revisions. Return exact version identifiers and eligible state.
2. Validate the combined baseline against the current sources. Freeze a deterministic manifest with digest, exact input versions, units, validity and source provenance.
3. Bind independent approval to that exact digest and the relevant company/asset scope. At publication, recheck authority, eligibility and expected head/version. Apply idempotent replay and preserve decision evidence.
4. Expose exact, current and effective/as-of queries, plus history and comparison. Retain historical reconstruction when a later baseline becomes effective.

**Acceptance.** A signed engineer discovers eligible sources, drafts and submits a manifest, and a distinct eligible reviewer authorizes publication. A second client retrieves the same digest and versions. A concurrent publish, stale expected head, wrong approval target or withdrawn source cannot silently advance the head. Test unauthorized source discovery and history. An approved software record preserves source status and provenance separately from engineering qualification.

### 3. Trusted Telemetry

1. Expose typed commissioning and lookup of sources, points and effective mappings/bindings. Validate current company, exact physical asset, engineering unit, authorized producer and reference validity.
2. Reuse native raw ingestion and idempotent replay. Preserve original observation timestamp, source sequence, raw payload/digest and binding provenance. Distinguish duplicate replay from conflicting payload.
3. Expose governed quality assessment and trusted publication. Retain the raw observation reference, assessment, scope, source binding version, unit and applicable time policy.
4. Return explicit eligibility and reasons for missing, stale, future-skewed, mismatched or rejected samples. Admit the late-data and binding-selection policy before implementation.

**Acceptance.** One signed producer ingests a valid sample and a repeat, then attempts conflicting replay. A qualified observation is published once. Another actor retrieves it after restart. Bad quality, revoked producer rights, expired mappings and incompatible units cannot produce a trusted result.

### 4. Authoritative Monitoring

1. Version and activate a rule with an explicit scope, unit, evaluation window and authorized input policy.
2. Retrieve the exact effective approved Planning target and trusted Telemetry reading through owner contracts. Resolve an accepted engineering envelope when required.
3. Calculate actual, expected and difference server-side. Persist evaluation identity, rule/version, source IDs, timestamps, units, quality, reason and durable result. Preserve the distinction between computed results and imported/recorded deviations.
4. Expose typed evaluation/result/history queries. Keep unknown, missing, stale and incompatible outcomes explicit.

**Acceptance.** A synthetic target of 100 and compatible trusted actual of 105 yield a reproducible +5. Repeating the same evidence follows deterministic replay policy. Unavailable or incompatible evidence never appears as a valid numeric deviation.

### 5. Correlated operational response

1. Define admitted evidence classes and versioned trigger policy. Create a correlated alarm or suspected leak under current scope. Persist correlation key, exact source evidence, trigger policy version and explanation.
2. Reuse permitted Alarm transitions and require current authority for acknowledgement or escalation. Resolve exact Workflow and Incident/Leak Detection target where required.
3. Return typed operator timeline, disposition and linked case evidence. Keep suspected, confirmed and resolved states distinct. A human decision is attributable to the current actor and is independent from any assertion of field execution.

**Acceptance.** Replay of one evidence trigger results in one permitted correlation outcome. Authorized actors acknowledge and escalate. Unauthorized actors cannot discover or mutate the alarm or linked case. A restarted client retrieves exact evidence and history.

### 6. Integrated GZ2 software proof

Run the complete journey with one pinned API revision, fresh PostgreSQL, synthetic fixtures and separate author, reviewer, producer, operator and foreign-company principals.

1. Discover and publish an engineering baseline. Create and independently approve the exact Planning target used by the rule.
2. Ingest a signed observation, apply the trusted publication contract and retrieve its raw-to-qualified lineage.
3. Evaluate the rule and retrieve the deviation with input versions and units. Raise the associated alarm and record a human decision.
4. Restart the application and retrieve exact immutable history. Repeat protected access with a revoked and a foreign actor. Supersede one relevant source version and verify the historical evaluation remains reconstructible.
5. Record exact runtime OpenAPI, PostgreSQL/Flyway evidence, raw case outcomes and run provenance. Qualify the backend software only after independent review of the full journey.

## 7. Definition of done and first handoff

For each increment, size the smallest coherent external journey and assign one accountable API owner. Record exact source paths, proposed REST shapes and errors, authority and transaction model, applicable migration, test cases and expected evidence before implementation.

| Gate | Required evidence |
|---|---|
| Functional | An independent client creates or discovers prerequisites, performs permitted operations with returned IDs and version tokens, and retrieves the durable final state. |
| Security | Signed JWT, current company/exact resource authority, non-disclosure of protected existence and totals, reviewer independence where applicable and revoke/DENY tests. |
| Persistence | Fresh PostgreSQL/Flyway/JPA proof where applicable. Constraints, forced rollback, replay, concurrency and restart readback cover the changed behavior. |
| Compatibility | Actual runtime OpenAPI and compatible existing client behavior, apart from explicitly approved changes. Publish exact routes, scopes, business errors and examples for frontend consumers. |
| Evidence | Exact source SHA, test cases and raw outcomes, workflow/run details and artifact provenance. Report implementation, test, software acceptance and industrial acceptance separately. |

**First handoff.** Prepare **T01**, then **T02** and **T03** in dependency order. For T01, settle period-code uniqueness, exact company and asset query predicates, REST shapes and the native test ledger. The first Planning increment is complete when T03 proves one signed author-to-independent-reviewer journey through persisted target readback. A task requires separate selection before implementation.

### T01 scope admission — 2026-11-10

**Owner decision.** Planning periods are company-owned. Period codes are unique within a company. Companies may independently reuse the same period code. The period's company is authoritative for its plans. T01 remains PLANNED, with implementation pending a separate selection and an exact execution envelope.

**API and authorization scope.** Apply the owner-backed company grant and, for plans, the exact Topology asset grant to existing period and plan create, detail, and list operations, including page totals. Resolve the actor on the server and verify the plan's asset belongs to the period's company. Apply equivalent controls to existing descendant reads that could bypass this boundary. Enforce current revocation and deny precedence. Restrict rows before pagination and counting. Use the same non-disclosing outcome for a protected foreign identifier and a missing one. T02 and T03 retain revision and target authoring, submission, and approval.

**Persistence.** The current `uk_hmr006_planning_period_code` index is global. Implement the company/code constraint in a new forward-only Flyway migration after the exact schema and JPA changes are admitted. Preserve prior migrations. Require explicit, validated company ownership and fail closed where ownership is unproven. Synthetic fixtures supply ownership for qualification.

**Acceptance.** Use signed native HTTP and PostgreSQL with two companies and two assets in one company. Prove that two companies may reuse a code, that a same-company duplicate is rejected, and that company and exact asset restrictions hold for creation, detail, list, and totals. Exercise foreign and unknown identifiers, revocation, descendant read bypass attempts, and restart readback. Verify actual Flyway/JPA constraints and the OpenAPI contract.

**Registration scope.** Only `doc/roadmap/ROADMAP.md` changes in this registration. Implementation still requires an exact source and test allowlist, migration filename, implementation commit message, and separate selection under the task execution protocol.

### T01 implementation envelope — 2026-11-10

**Baseline.** Main `fbb21945f4c3f3172042d7b6df9f4d94489f75c2` passed [Documentation Validation #978](https://github.com/CHOUABBIA-AMINE/HidraAPI/actions/runs/42853830035). Its source baseline `e7afe49a46b56c2cee637f56ea855c8d540c72b0` passed [Full CI #1176, attempt 2](https://github.com/CHOUABBIA-AMINE/HidraAPI/actions/runs/42841011012/attempts/2). T01 remains PLANNED. The implementation message is `feat(planning): enforce company and asset scope`. Reserve `src/main/resources/db/migration/V20261110_002__planning_company_scope.sql`. Refresh the exact HEAD, migration ordering and evidence before implementation.

**Ownership and transaction.** Planning owns the immutable period company and company/code invariant. A plan derives its company from its period. Party establishes current company eligibility, Topology establishes current asset ownership, Identity evaluates current grants, and Organization retains responsibility and unit eligibility. Consume owner contracts through application boundaries. Resolve the actor from the authenticated request. Use a single transaction per operation and keep checked evidence current for the transaction. For reads, build the authorized company and exact company/type/asset tuples first, and constrain both SQL rows and count before pagination. Missing, inactive, ambiguous or unavailable owner evidence denies access. For writes, bind the owner and grant checks to the write transaction. Keep exact permit and deny precedence. Current JWT or a global route grant alone does not establish company or asset access.

**Supported ownership evidence.** Resolve PIPELINE_SYSTEM through the immutable Foundation system-owner record. Resolve PIPELINE through its exact system relationship and the verified system owner. Resolve FACILITY through its explicit current owner. Validate the corresponding asset lifecycle and active eligible company. Existing supported asset types remain meaningful where these owner records prove their scope. The owner lookup stays in Topology. Do not infer ownership from an identifier prefix, a Planning snapshot, or the caller's grant.

**Persistence and API.** Add the company association using a forward migration. Enforce same-company code uniqueness in PostgreSQL, preserve period date and catalog checks, and exclude unproven legacy ownership from scoped reads. The migration must require company ownership for new writes without inventing a historical owner. Replace the global uniqueness rule only with the database-backed company/code rule. Plans join through their period, and revision, nomination, target and approval detail reads inherit the same plan boundary. Cover POST aliases for period and plan creation, GET list and detail operations for periods and operational plans, and the existing revision, nomination, target and approval reads. Existing descendant mutation behavior belongs to its respective task. Preserve responsible-unit validation and route permissions. Accept an optional legacy actor field only if it matches the signed actor when supplied. It cannot confer authority. Return a uniform non-disclosing missing-resource outcome for foreign and missing protected identifiers, and a conflict for a proven same-company duplicate.

**Unresolved API compatibility gate.** `CreatePlanningPeriodRequest` has no company selector. T01 requires explicit validated ownership. A new required request property on either existing v1 period-create route fails the enforced OpenAPI compatibility rule. No authoritative selected-company context is established for these routes. The owner must decide the versioning and legacy behavior before implementation. Proposed approach is a versioned scoped period-create contract with an explicit company, plus an explicitly approved fail-closed policy for v1 callers without a company. Retain the compatibility gate and document the actual behavior. Do not hide a required field or select an implicit company to satisfy CI.

#### T01 implementation file envelope

### T01 period-create API decision — 2026-11-10

**Decision.** This entry resolves the period-create compatibility gate above. Add `POST /api/v2/planning/periods` with a dedicated request requiring a nonblank `companyPartyId`. Carry over the supported business fields from period creation. Resolve the actor from the authenticated principal and validate the selected company's eligibility and the actor's current scoped create grant inside the write transaction. Use the existing `planning:periods:execute` route permission in addition to the scoped grant. Catalog the new route under that permission.

**Legacy behavior.** Preserve `POST /api/v1/planning/periods`, `POST /api/v1/planning/create-planning-period`, and the v1 request schema. Both aliases deny otherwise valid authenticated requests with a generic `403` when a verified company context is absent. There is currently no authoritative company context for either alias. Unauthenticated requests follow the existing `401` behavior. A denied request makes no write. Never derive the company from a raw token claim, a sole grant, or the legacy actor field. Document the v1 denial and the v2 replacement in the runtime OpenAPI contract and retain strict compatibility validation.

**Additional T01 implementation paths.** The existing envelope remains in effect with the following additions. Platform changes are scoped to registering, enforcing and cataloging the new Planning route. Existing permission naming already derives `planning:periods:execute` from its path and method.

Verify that the route catalog lists the v2 operation under the same permission enforced at runtime. Confirm the v1 request schema and both route mappings are preserved and the generated runtime OpenAPI declares the required v2 company field.

**Contract.** Add `POST /api/v1/planning/operational-plans/{planId}/revisions`, `POST /api/v1/planning/revisions/{revisionId}/targets` and `PUT /api/v1/planning/targets/{targetId}`. Retain the existing revision metadata PATCH contract. Require its current company/exact-asset author grant through Identity permission `planning:scoped-plan:author`, alongside the derived route permission. Generate revision and target identities, revision sequence, DRAFT status and version timestamps on the server. The first revision has no base. Later revisions use the plan's current terminal revision as their base. An existing DRAFT or SUBMITTED head blocks another draft.

**Concurrency.** Acquire the Planning plan lock before revision and target locks. Revision creation compares `expectedPlanUpdatedAt`. Target changes compare `expectedRevisionUpdatedAt`, and target replacement also compares `expectedTargetUpdatedAt`. Advance the revision token after every target edit. Existing metadata PATCH continues to compare its revision token. Use PostgreSQL microsecond timestamps and reject stale, noncurrent or non-DRAFT edits with a conflict. Preserve atomic rollback and existing database uniqueness/parent constraints.

**Target meaning.** Targets use the exact authorized plan asset, the current active TARGET_TYPE representation policy, optional same-revision scenario/nomination, and a nonempty effective window contained in the period. Numeric targets require an active Telemetry unit. When a point is supplied, Telemetry verifies its active source/device/point, representation, exact asset binding and binding coverage for the complete target window. Numeric units must match the point's current unit. TEXT targets keep their existing representation rules. This stage introduces no unit conversion or industrial default values.

Java Maven verification in the alternate lane was skipped by the workflow; successful mandatory partitions and evidence gate, not that skipped alternative, support T02 software acceptance. **Selected task and commit budget.** The owner selected the next registered T03 stage. This admission is the single optional roadmap/approval registration commit for T03, using exact message `docs(roadmap): register T03 approval and execution scope`; it is not a source implementation or operational acceptance. No additional task approval or documentation registration commit is planned. Follow the required post-publication CI startup/stop rule for each separate publication, without auto-advancing to T04.

**Bounded semantics and owner policy.** Planning owns the plan, revision and target lifecycle; Workflow owns the definition, instance, task, transition, action and immutable decision evidence; Identity owns current actor/grant authority; Party/Topology preserve current company and exact asset ownership. Submit only the current DRAFT revision whose parent plan and period are eligible. Verify a current scoped author grant, exact target/plan association, optimistic revision/plan tokens and an active, version-matched Workflow definition bound to exactly \`planning\` and the registered \`PLAN_REVISION\` target/purpose. Require actual independent eligible reviewer assignment; never create an implicit reviewer, permissive wildcard, synthetic production definition or default approval. A workflow ID alone is not approval. Discover/validate actual Workflow definition, first step, assignment and decision policy through Workflow-owned contracts. Retain DRAFT target values and records as historical evidence while freezing edits on submission.

**Decision guard.** The execute and any generic Workflow bypass must enforce current authenticated human reviewer eligibility, up-to-date company and exact asset grant, correct submitted-current revision, reviewer distinct from submitter, current unrevoked Workflow permission and assignment, exact instance/target/definition binding and nonterminal task with CAS token. A valid terminal APPROVE atomically updates revision/plan approval pointers and activates only that revision's targets; previously active targets are superseded where applicable. A terminal REJECT records rejection without activation. Intermediate nonterminal Workflow steps retain SUBMITTED Planning state. Repeated/stale, self-review, withdrawn, superseded and unauthorized actions fail without writes. A failed Planning update rolls back Workflow action/task/history/instance changes as one database transaction, including forced failures. Do not rely on caller-supplied role names or stale permission snapshots, and do not expose protected target existence through Workflow query/action paths.

**API admission.** Add \`POST /api/v1/planning/revisions/{revisionId}/submit\` with a validated explicit request for the current revision token, active definition/version and verified independent reviewer assignment; return the persisted revision, instance/task references and current concurrency evidence. Preserve existing \`GET /api/v1/planning/revisions/{revisionId}/approval\` and \`POST /api/v1/planning/revisions/{revisionId}/approval/actions/{transitionId}/execute\` wire shapes, changing internal validation only. Keep canonical ProblemDetail, server-derived actor identity, no direct JPA from REST, and non-disclosing foreign/missing references. Current scoped \`planning:scoped-plan:author\` remains the submission business gate; the distinct decision gate is \`planning:scoped-plan:review\` with current company/exact asset checks and Workflow's required transition permission. Register the review permission without seeding business grants. Do not broaden legacy REST response data or weaken backward compatibility.

A normalized nomination code is unique per revision among new governed rows and may not collide with an existing code under that revision. Same command ID with a different payload returns conflict. Serialize authoring on the plan/revision and disposition on the nomination, with database uniqueness backing the governed business key and one terminal decision. Keep updates, receipt and history atomic. Use non-disclosing unavailable responses for missing or out-of-scope parents, nominations and movement endpoints. Keep ordinary validation errors and state conflicts distinct for authorized requests.

**Verified starting point at `03c0fc4`.** T20 owns immutable OBSERVED interval receipts and captured measurements with `acceptedForCustody=false`. Existing Custody JPA entities include measurement period, reconciliation, quantity calculation, ticket, ticket line, discrepancy and measurement snapshot; their presence does not establish an implemented fiscal lifecycle. `CustodyApplicationService` currently exposes period/ticket/discrepancy creation, and `SpringCustodyController` exposes only those legacy writes and capabilities. Existing statuses are period OPEN/LOCKED/CALCULATED/APPROVED/CLOSED/REOPENED/CANCELLED; reconciliation DRAFT/IN_PROGRESS/BALANCED/DISCREPANCY_FOUND/APPROVED/CLOSED/CANCELLED; ticket DRAFT/SUBMITTED/UNDER_REVIEW/APPROVED/REJECTED/CANCELLED/CLOSED; discrepancy OPEN/UNDER_REVIEW/ACCEPTED/REJECTED/RESOLVED/CLOSED/CANCELLED. Do not treat these enums as implemented transitions. Existing `CustodyTransferTicketReferenceValidation` checks actor, Workflow, Audit, batch and calculation references; retain those guarantees. Existing `numeric(18,6)` measurement and calculation columns constrain exact arithmetic.

**Bounded domain and decision policy.** Custody owns the measurement period, reconciliation snapshot, transfer ticket, discrepancy disposition and correction chain. Telemetry owns qualified immutable measurement evidence; Identity owns current grants; Topology owns asset/company; Party owns eligibility; Workflow owns independent decision evidence; Audit owns audit references. One synthetic facility-scoped GZ2 gas period, one configured observed-volume unit and qualified T20 receipts only. No standard-volume conversion, physical correction factors, calorific or fiscal certification, multiphase, numerical solver, SCADA or production integration. Require explicit signed actor and exact current company/transfer-point grants separately for period/ticket/discrepancy reads, reconciliation, discrepancy disposition, finalization and correction. Deny protected existence, counts, history and replay before revealing details. Resolve ownership from Topology and match the immutable T20 scope; historical authorized reads retain original evidence.

**Lifecycle and invariants.** Reconcile only an OPEN period with a nonempty deterministic set of eligible T20 interval receipts from the same period, agreement, transfer point, company, meter/product basis and exact unit. Require no overlap/duplicate contribution; snapshot receipt IDs, evidence versions, quantity and unit, selection algorithm/version, actor and time. Aggregate exact decimal quantities without rounding. The initial supported ticket quantity equals the selected observed total; record a deterministic zero difference and 0% when denominator is positive, with an explicit zero-denominator policy. If an existing ticket quantity differs, record a discrepancy and block finalization until an authorized explicit disposition; never silently adjust measured evidence. Reconciliation freezes its input set. New measurements or eligibility changes after reconciliation cannot rewrite the snapshot; require an explicit new version or fail closed. Ticket and period state changes are monotonic under the admitted transition table; a terminal ticket is immutable. Finalization requires balanced or explicitly disposed reconciliation, a bound eligible ticket and calculation, no unresolved discrepancy, exact current authority, and independent decision evidence where a fiscal/official approval is asserted. No self-approval, generic Workflow bypass, stale decision, stale version or unverified approval. Preserve existing status meanings; do not mark `official=true` or `acceptedForCustody=true` merely because T20 source was qualified. The owner may implement a bounded software-finalized state without claiming legally certified custody transfer.

**Correction policy.** No in-place edit to finalized measured values, reconciliation evidence or issued ticket quantities. An authorized correction requires original finalized ticket ID, reason, actor, exact evidence and expected current version; create a new superseding ticket/reconciliation/calculation snapshot and an append-only correction link, preserving the original, full chain and original approval evidence. Recheck eligibility and authority for the correction transaction; preserve historical source lineage without requalifying old evidence. Enforce a single active successor per corrected head, unique correction command ID, deterministic replay and conflict on changed payload. The superseding record must complete the same independent finalization gate; a pending correction cannot masquerade as an effective finalized ticket. Prevent cycles, cross-period links, cross-company substitutions and concurrent double successors.

No free-form evaluator, unit conversion, time-series aggregation, simulation, automated operating decision or industrial calibration. **REST and authority.** Exact base `/api/v1/analytics/companies/{companyId}/facilities/{facilityId}/deviation-metric-runs`. POST method `execute(String, String, ExecuteDeviationMetricRunRequest)` takes `definitionVersionId` and `evaluationId` only, returns 201 for a newly persisted terminal result and 200 for exact replay. GET method `read(String, String, String)` on base plus `/{runId}` returns 200 for the committed projection. POST requires explicit current `analytics:deviation-metric:execute` and `analytics:deviation-metric:read`, GET requires current read; each permission needs direct current permits on `CUSTOM analytics-company:{companyId}` and `FACILITY {facilityId}`, existing native LOCAL actor verification, and Identity deny precedence. Both paths also require current owner-authorized Monitoring READ for the exact T11 rule and same owner company/facility. Authorize the requested scope before protected run, definition or source disclosure. Return generic non-disclosing 404 for absent/foreign/revoked scope or protected evidence, 400 for malformed IDs, and 422 for authorized unsupported/inactive/version-invalid/unit-incompatible metric configuration. A known authorized non-COMPUTED Monitoring result persists `FAILED / SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE` and source outcome, with no metric value; a computed result that cannot be represented exactly in numeric(18,6) persists `FAILED / VALUE_OUT_OF_RANGE`. Never substitute zero or round silently. Reuse existing platform error mapping for malformed and denied inputs; define the typed 422 response locally in the new controller. Use no list or count operation.

Store stable versions/identifiers for historical readback, with no re-resolution to a newer definition/rule or recalculation during GET. Expose only sealed lineage approved by both owner checks. Exact concurrent/repeated requests share the same run ID. **Verified prerequisites and gaps.** Existing `RegisterDocumentUseCase`,
`UploadDocumentBinaryVersionUseCase`, `DownloadDocumentVersionContentUseCase`,
`DocumentContentTransferService`, `LocalDocumentBinaryStorageAdapter` and
document/version/storage/link persistence provide real content transfer, SHA-256,
atomic database orchestration and confirmed-rollback cleanup. An unknown commit
outcome preserves the candidate blob for reconciliation. Existing constraints
require same-document current version, unique positive version number,
non-self supersession, active catalog families and exact uploader identity.
Existing `DocumentsOwnedTargetLookup` exports owner-controlled identity/code/label
and includes Topology FACILITY, but does not prove owning company or current scoped
authority. Current download resolves a version/storage and opens content without a
record-aware company/facility authorization check. There is no scoped controlled
discovery, version/link history, acceptance or supersession command. Generic
Workbench configuration could expose Documents counts/rows without record scope.
These are the bounded T24 gaps. The GZ2 signed fixture can restart an independent
app JVM, but needs an explicit persistent per-fixture storage root/provider and
multipart/binary helpers. Existing Documents unit/PostgreSQL tests construct the
services directly; their constructor updates are listed below.

**Chosen first scope and acceptance semantics.** One company and one active
Topology FACILITY, with a newly registered Document whose owner tuple is
`topology / FACILITY / facilityId`. Enroll it atomically through the new scoped
create route in a Documents-owned immutable scope binding. Existing non-enrolled
records retain their legacy command semantics and are excluded from the new
scoped queries. Each controlled exact version can have immutable evidence links
only to that same facility, with an active `DOCUMENT_LINK_ROLE`. One primary
version-specific owner link is appended automatically upon successful acceptance.
This establishes the reusable Documents foundation for later T17/T25 integrations;
target-specific HSE/Reporting attachment behavior belongs to its consuming task.

Here acceptance is an explicit Documents custodian decision backed by the
`documents:controlled:accept` permission, actor, reason, exact byte hash and
request identity. It publishes a DRAFT content version as CURRENT and the
Document as ACTIVE, without setting a Workflow approval reference or an APPROVED
state. The acceptor must differ from both the document creator and the uploader.
A first acceptance requires no current version. Supersession atomically accepts
a higher numbered DRAFT of the same document, marks the prior CURRENT as
SUPERSEDED with `supersededByVersionId`, advances
`Document.currentVersionId` and appends the decision and successor's exact target
link. Existing upload/approval metadata is retained. Domain policy returns the
permitted version transition using immutable existing domain records.
`Document.currentVersionId` is the sole current-version pointer; decision history
is append-only. A version's bytes, storage/hash/size, uploader and original
target evidence are frozen once accepted. Controlled decisions provide evidence
acceptance; content engineering validity requires its applicable owner process.

**Application and authorization envelope.** New Documents port and application
service coordinate the existing registration and content use cases. A shared
record guard uses the controlled JDBC repository internally, avoiding a dependency
cycle through the version repository. The only importer of the new Identity and
Topology contracts is `ControlledDocumentOwnerAccessAdapter`. Identity supplies
the verified LOCAL actor and permissions `documents:controlled:create`,
`documents:controlled:write`, `documents:controlled:read`,
`documents:controlled:accept`. Require direct current permits for each requested
capability on both `CUSTOM documents-company:{companyId}` and
`FACILITY facilityId`, plus current assertion/effective-deny evaluation.
Read is required with each mutation. Resolve current active facility ownership
through Topology after authorizing the requested scope and require the owner
company to equal the bound company. On ownership change, the former owner loses
controlled access and the new owner is not automatically granted historical
Documents access. Recheck grants on each request, including historical byte reads.

The guard covers both metadata upload aliases, binary upload, both target-link
aliases, known-version byte download, document/storage existence exports and the
controlled repository write path. Resolve hidden scope internally, then authorize
before any existence/hash/history/availability disclosure or blob access.
Legacy routes retain their transport permission requirements and gain this
additional record fence for enrolled records. New native routes call the same
guarded services. An authenticated broad legacy permission must not bypass a
controlled scope. Metadata-only upload cannot attach another document's blob to
an enrolled document. Scope the storage guard to any storage object referenced
by an enrolled version, including mixed references. Generic Workbench Documents
entity exposure is disabled, including explicit configured exposure, because its
list/search/count/detail pipeline cannot apply the controlled record predicate.
This is an intentional compatibility change for generic Documents Workbench reads.

**Exact REST surface.** The base `B` below means
`/api/v1/documents/companies/{companyId}/facilities/{facilityId}/controlled-documents`.
Every path carries current scoped authorization, exact document/version parenting
and native LOCAL authentication.

| Method and path | Exact controller method | Request/response and behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| POST B | `create(String,String,ControlledDocumentRequests.Create)` | Explicit requestId, code, titleFr, documentTypeId and classificationId; server derives owner and actor. 201 new / 200 exact replay. |
| GET B | `discover(String,String,Integer,Integer,String)` | page 0+, size 1–100, optional code filter; authorized documents only with total, current version/hash and stable code/id ordering. |
| GET B/{documentId} | `detail(String,String,String)` | Document identity, bound facility and authoritative current version. |
| GET B/{documentId}/versions | `versions(String,String,String,Integer,Integer)` | Scoped page of exact draft/current/superseded version IDs, numbers, hashes, sizes and dates. |
| GET B/{documentId}/links | `links(String,String,String,Integer,Integer)` | Scoped page of immutable exact-version facility links and decision lineage, ordered linkedAt/id. |
| POST B/{documentId}/versions/upload | `upload(String,String,String,UploadDocumentBinaryVersionRequest,MultipartFile)` | Reuse multipart metadata+file shape. Body documentId must match path. 200 typed draft version; existing version-number uniqueness resolves concurrent uploads, confirmed rollback cleans only the losing blob. |
| GET B/{documentId}/versions/{versionId}/content | `content(String,String,String,String)` | Reuse attachment content response with exact bytes/length and SHA-256 ETag; available historical accepted versions remain retrievable. |
| POST B/{documentId}/versions/{versionId}/accept | `accept(String,String,String,String,ControlledDocumentRequests.Accept)` | requestId, reason and linkRoleId; require current head null; 201 decision / 200 exact replay. |
| POST B/{documentId}/versions/{versionId}/supersede | `supersede(String,String,String,String,ControlledDocumentRequests.Supersede)` | versionId is successor; requestId, reason, linkRoleId and expectedCurrentVersionId pin the predecessor; 201 decision / 200 replay, 409 stale head or payload conflict. |

All nested response schema names must be explicitly prefixed ControlledDocument
to avoid the global `Source`/`History` schema collisions. Keep common configured
null omission and typed optional fields consistent. Malformed inputs use 400,
authorized state/duplicate conflicts 409, missing/foreign/revoked protected scope
a generic non-disclosing 404, content-integrity failure a typed 409 or existing
storage failure mapping. A rejected acceptance never advances current state or
creates a successful link/decision.

**Physical state, concurrency and storage proof.** Add
`hidra_documents_controlled_scope` keyed by document ID and
`hidra_documents_controlled_decision` keyed by decision ID. Scope binds company,
facility, create requestId/payload digest, actor and time. Decision pins
document, version, optional predecessor, requestId/payload digest, actor/reason,
action, exact checksum/length, owner snapshots, selected linkRoleId/link ID and
time. Use restrictive same-document references, a unique scoped create request,
a unique document request, a unique accepted version and a unique non-null
predecessor to prevent branching. Lock the existing document row for accept and
supersede and check exact replay before mutable head eligibility. Replaying a
successful request returns its recorded decision even after another successor;
contradictory payload returns 409. Serialize pending create identity before
inserting a document and use database uniqueness as the second guard.
Flush pending JPA writes before JDBC references; clear/refresh stale state
before projecting results. Never perform SELECT FOR UPDATE/SHARE inside a
read-only transaction.

Migration guards apply to enrolled records, with separate PL/pgSQL branches for
each row type. Prove correct parent/current/head relation, allowed DRAFT→CURRENT
and CURRENT→SUPERSEDED transitions with a matching decision in the same
transaction, increasing successor number, valid checksum/length and immutable
acceptance/links. Freeze accepted storage/version metadata, restrict content
reparenting and guard DELETE/TRUNCATE. Preserve existing history and constraints;
seed permission definitions only. Reuse the existing SHA-256 storage provider
and rollback synchronization. Verify physical bytes against version/storage
metadata before acceptance and before delivering controlled content, closing
streams on every failure. Use one opened file handle to check and rewind for
delivery so the verified bytes are the returned bytes; admit a Documents-only
extension on the binary port for that operation. The new implementation must
preserve the existing store/open/delete methods and their callers. Configure
synthetic storage via an isolated temporary directory shared by both app JVMs
within the test, retain the same provider ID, and clean it when the scenario ends.

#### T17 owned boundary, admitted synthetic journey and explicit policy

HSE owns `HseCase`, `HseCorrectivePreventiveAction`, `HseClosure`,
HSE evidence, effectiveness and terminal state. The existing
`HseCase` → `HseCorrectivePreventiveAction` association, HSE-owned case
status history and HMR-082/096/097 constraints remain authoritative.
Identity owns actual current grants and actors; Topology owns current
FACILITY/company identity; Incident owns T16 investigation/review; Documents
owns T24 accepted immutable version bytes/decisions; Workflow owns review
definitions, target bindings and independent decisions. HSE consumes only
new explicit provider-owned `application.contract.hse` scalar contracts
through its sole new HSE owner-access adapter. No foreign private domain,
infrastructure/persistence, generic Workbench bypass, new autonomous action,
simulation or direct industrial-control integration is authorized.

**First supported flow:** one synthetic GZ2 company, one active Topology
FACILITY, one eligible reviewed T16 Incident on that same facility, and
one or more new HSE-enrolled cases/CAPAs. All new enrolled case creation
uses the exact incident/company/facility proof and persists an immutable
HSE-owned scope binding atomically with the HSE case. The old generic HSE
case/CAPA objects have no reliable company scope field; do **not**
retroactively treat existing rows as scoped, infer company from organization
hierarchy, or migrate pre-existing records. Original un-enrolled API behavior
is retained where currently admitted. A T17-enrolled row must be hidden from
ALL existing legacy unscoped case/CAPA list/count/detail routes and may not
be created, mutated or closed through context-free legacy aliases.
Non-enrolled legacy policy remains a separate T29 resource-read coverage
concern and is not asserted as globally qualified by T17.

**Human sequence:**
`PROPOSED → APPROVED → IN_PROGRESS → COMPLETED → VERIFIED → CLOSED`
for newly enrolled CAPAs. The assign command is the approved CAPA owner's
transition from APPROVED to IN_PROGRESS. Rejected/inapplicable decisions
and legacy statuses remain meaningful; this first enrolled flow does not
rewrite old CAPAs or manufacture state-machine rules for those records.
A CAPA approval requires the actual current Workflow `HSE_CAPA` decision,
not just `caseMatches`, `taskMatches` or an arbitrary workflow ID.
Only an authorized distinct verifier may assert an EFFECTIVE finding with
an immutable accepted document-version link, reason and time. An
INEFFECTIVE/INDETERMINATE outcome is persistable evidence but does NOT
set VERIFIED or authorize closure; a follow-up may require a new versioned
review attempt. The HSE CASE closure requires every enrolled required CAPA
to have a persisted effective VERIFIED decision, a linked exact retained
evidence version, impact/evidence attestation traceable to persisted HSE
sources, a non-empty reason, and an independent, exact-target approved
Workflow `HSE_CASE` decision. Closure atomically records actual
HSE closure, status history, admitted Workflow decision/receipt and terminal
CAPA state without trusting caller-provided `impactAssessed`,
`capaCompleted` or `evidenceReviewed` booleans as authoritative facts.
No invented physical effectiveness threshold or real-site calibration
is required. Optional regulatory review retains its existing explicit,
owner-governed applicability rather than defaulting to an invented rule.

**Authorization and consistency:**
register explicit sensitive permissions
`hse:capa:create`, `hse:capa:read`, `hse:capa:execute`,
`hse:capa:review`, `hse:capa:close` without seeding any user grants.
For every enrolled command/read/count/history/replay, authenticate the
current actor and check explicit CURRENT direct permits and effective
policy at both the company-specific CUSTOM scope and exact FACILITY
scope, with deny precedence; verify currently ACTIVE facility ownership
matches the captured company and the Incident/Document/Workflow owner
references. No role-name, DTO claim, historical receipt, Workbench row,
stale session or user-supplied actor can authorize a transition. Check
current authority **before** revealing existence; recheck inside the
lock-capable transaction for mutation or protected disclosure.
Do not run current-grant `SELECT FOR SHARE/UPDATE` in a read-only transaction.
A later company transfer, revoked actor, withdrawn evidence or mismatched
current owner must fail closed; immutable historical evidence remains
reconstructible for an independently authorized reviewer.

Use exact `requestId` + canonical payload digest per enrolled
case/CAPA command, unique request/case, unique sequential revision,
`expectedVersion` compare-and-swap and actual HSE parent/CAPA row locks.
Matching replay is read-authorized and returns the same immutable receipt;
a different payload for a reused key or stale expected version is
`409` without extra writes. Lock ordering is HSE case then CAPA then
HSE event/version, not the reverse. Source owner lookups and current
company/asset authorization must precede any new HSE commit. Commit
actual HSE record, event, evidence, verifier findings and closure together;
rollback must leave no partial approved, verified or closed outcome.
Use stable paging/order and no existence/count/history side channel.

**PostgreSQL migration shape:** next free version as currently observed
`V20261118_002__t17_hse_capa_governed_lifecycle.sql`; rescan versions at
the next execution lease and never overwrite `V20261118_001` or any other
applied migration. Exactly six proposed NEW HSE-owned, non-JPA tables:
`hidra_hse_t17_case_scope` (immutable company/facility/Incident and create
digest), `hidra_hse_t17_capa_state` (one locked revision per CAPA),
`hidra_hse_t17_capa_event` (immutable request/transition/actor event),
`hidra_hse_t17_capa_evidence` (immutable accepted exact Documents version,
checksum/length), `hidra_hse_t17_capa_verification` (append-only reviewer
finding and evidence linkage), `hidra_hse_t17_case_close_receipt`
(exact Workflow decision and HSE closure ID).
Foreign keys are permitted only to HSE-owned parent rows where lifecycle
appropriate, with explicit RESTRICT, sequence uniqueness, non-null/shape
checks and non-deletion/immutable guards. Incident/Topology/Documents/
Workflow references remain scalar IDs plus owner-validated immutable
snapshots, **not** cross-owner table writes or speculative physical FKs.
The migration inserts permission catalogue identities only, never
company-specific grants or real data. Require physical deferred consistency
guards so legacy/direct SQL cannot bypass enrolled transition,
case-close/receipt and evidence/verification relationships.

#### T17 proposed signed native HTTP contract — 13 exact operations

| Method | Proposed path | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| `POST` | `/api/v1/hse/companies/{companyId}/facilities/{facilityId}/cases/from-incident` | Create one enrolled HSE case bound to approved T16 Incident and active FACILITY/company. |
| `GET` | `/api/v1/hse/companies/{companyId}/facilities/{facilityId}/cases` | Company+facility scoped, stable ordered list/count; no foreign/legacy leak. |
| `GET` | `/api/v1/hse/companies/{companyId}/facilities/{facilityId}/cases/{caseId}` | Authorized case detail with scope/incident/workflow snapshots. |
| `POST` | `/api/v1/hse/companies/{companyId}/facilities/{facilityId}/cases/{caseId}/capas` | Create exact parent-bound PROPOSED CAPA with approved action-type family. |
| `GET` | `/api/v1/hse/companies/{companyId}/facilities/{facilityId}/cases/{caseId}/capas` | Scoped CAPA list/count and current status/verification summary. |
| `GET` | `/api/v1/hse/companies/{companyId}/facilities/{facilityId}/cases/{caseId}/capas/{capaId}` | Exact scoped CAPA and latest immutable decision/evidence refs. |
| `POST` | `/api/v1/hse/companies/{companyId}/facilities/{facilityId}/cases/{caseId}/capas/{capaId}/approve` | Independent Workflow-backed approval and expected revision. |
| `POST` | `/api/v1/hse/companies/{companyId}/facilities/{facilityId}/cases/{caseId}/capas/{capaId}/assign` | Eligible current owner assignment; transition to IN_PROGRESS only after approval. |
| `POST` | `/api/v1/hse/companies/{companyId}/facilities/{facilityId}/cases/{caseId}/capas/{capaId}/evidence` | Append exact accepted T24 document-version evidence. |
| `POST` | `/api/v1/hse/companies/{companyId}/facilities/{facilityId}/cases/{caseId}/capas/{capaId}/complete` | Owner completion with stored evidence/expected revision. |
| `POST` | `/api/v1/hse/companies/{companyId}/facilities/{facilityId}/cases/{caseId}/capas/{capaId}/verify` | Independent human effectiveness outcome, linked evidence, reason and revision. |
| `POST` | `/api/v1/hse/companies/{companyId}/facilities/{facilityId}/cases/{caseId}/close` | Exact independent Workflow HSE_CASE decision and authoritative persisted closure. |
| `GET` | `/api/v1/hse/companies/{companyId}/facilities/{facilityId}/cases/{caseId}/history` | Scoped immutable ordered case/CAPA/verification/closure history. |

All paths above are **TARGET/PROPOSED**, not currently implemented
endpoints. Each controller method must have a deliberate typed inbound
port, concrete native signature, explicit authorization, validation and
consistent 400/401/403/404/409/5xx error handling. Refusals do not
leak protected record IDs, counts, source history or the existence of
foreign documents. Reuse the existing production exception mapping;
do not invent a second error format. A case is an HSE aggregate, not an
Incident/Workflow/Document aggregate. No binary HSE download or duplicate
Document storage is created: authorized evidence retrieval remains
Documents-owned under T24 authorization.

#### T25 exact-source gap and chosen workflow

`SpringReportingController` exposes create/request/queue and metadata artifact POST
aliases plus capabilities. `ReportingApplicationService.queueReportRun` checks the
existing request, active definition, template lineage, required concrete parameters
and Workflow where configured, then writes QUEUED. Its `generateReportArtifact` accepts
caller-supplied filename, size, checksum and existing Documents reference and persists
artifact metadata. It does not perform deterministic rendering or read exact bytes.
`ReportingDocumentReferenceContract` checks only document/storage existence.
`ReportingWorkflowApprovalQueryService.approved` checks completion, target module/ID
and existence of some APPROVE action; T25 needs one exact bound action and an
independent reviewer. `ReportingAccessAuthorizationContract` is the legacy access-policy
lookup, not the native current actor company/FACILITY fence. T23
`DeviationMetricRunApplicationService.read` already authorizes the retained result
and its source, while T24 `ControlledDocumentsApplicationService` already supplies
facility-scoped create/upload/independent accept and verified exact-version content.
`DocumentContentTransferService` includes rollback cleanup for a new blob and retains
unknown-commit objects for owner reconciliation. Preserve those semantics when composing
transactions.

**Scope.** One manual `GZ2_ABSOLUTE_DEVIATION_JSON_V1` report type, one approval-required
active Reporting definition, one active linked template revision, one required typed
`metricRunId` REFERENCE parameter. Template v1 specifies a fixed field set/order with
canonical UTF-8 JSON and LF, exact numeric rules (normalize decimal trailing zeros and
use plain decimal notation), and UTC source timestamps. Render the immutable T23
COMPLETED receipt including run, metric definition version, method, value, unit,
evaluation ID, rule/revision, approved Planning target revision/approval and trusted
reading provenance. Freeze that allowed projection and hash at request admission.
Recheck source access and exact projection at render. Reject failed, unavailable,
wrong-facility or mismatched receipts. Output bytes exclude wall-clock generation
time, actor name, internal storage paths and random run identifiers. Arbitrary
templates, caller-supplied input values, scheduling, distribution, release, simulation
and other formats are outside this implementation scope.

Reporting owns report request, eligibility, run state, frozen projection and output
receipt. Analytics owns the metric and its input eligibility. Workflow owns the human
decision. Identity owns current authority and Topology owns facility identity. Documents
owns managed version, independent custodian acceptance and binary content. Each source
owner exposes a narrow application contract consumed through Reporting's outbound
adapter. Reuse existing Reporting request, parameter, run and output records and the
HMR-013/048/057/093 guards. A new Reporting-owned lifecycle receipt extends them and
pins exact external references without cross-owner foreign keys.

**Owner configuration.** Synthetic fixtures supply an eligible definition/template,
its required parameter, a `REPORT_REQUEST` / `REPORT_APPROVAL` Workflow binding,
reviewer assignment, active Documents type/classification/link role and existing
storage provider. Use fixed server-side definition/profile codes and resolve exact
active owner records before use. The migration provisions permission identities only.
No user/role grants or industry template defaults are installed. Test actors receive
explicit current grants at both scopes for their operations. Requester renders after a
different Workflow reviewer approves. A custodian distinct from document creator and
uploader accepts and seals. Existing Workflow and Documents owner semantics determine
actor eligibility; caller actor, owner, state, checksum, filename, mime or byte values
cannot substitute for owner evidence.

#### HTTP and transaction contract

Base path `/api/v1/reporting/companies/{companyId}/facilities/{facilityId}`.
Register five distinct native tuples and use globally distinctive T25 DTO/schema names.

| Method and suffix | Input or output | Authority and state |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /report-requests` | `T25SubmitReport(requestKey, definitionId, templateVersionId, metricRunId)` → scoped request ID and frozen input lineage | `reporting:scoped-report:submit`; validate template/profile and source, store SUBMITTED and parameter in one transaction; 201 on new, 200 on exact replay. |
| `POST /report-requests/{requestId}/render` | `T25RenderReport(requestKey, workflowInstanceId, workflowActionId)` → run ID, state, typed failure or draft handoff | `reporting:scoped-report:render` and originating actor; validate one exact independent Workflow approval, current preflight and T24 create/write capacity. Synchronous bounded render. The exact-payload retry returns the same outcome. |
| `GET /report-runs/{runId}` | T25 state, exact template and source lineage, safe failure code or authorized publication details | `reporting:scoped-report:read` with current company and FACILITY authorization before lookup. |
| `POST /report-runs/{runId}/seal` | `T25SealReport(requestKey)` → exact accepted output and hash | `reporting:scoped-report:seal` plus T24 accept and read. The server accepts the recorded draft only. Independent T24 custodian and same transaction with report output/terminal update. |
| `GET /report-runs/{runId}/content` | Exact `application/json` attachment, length and checksum from sealed receipt | `reporting:scoped-report:read` and T24 current read. Verify exact document/version/acceptance, full bounded binary length and SHA-256 before response. |

Use Identity current native LOCAL actor, direct paired CUSTOM
`reporting-company:{companyId}` and FACILITY permits, policy PERMIT at both scopes,
and current Topology ownership. Apply scoped authority before protected existence,
metadata or bytes. Preserve the existing denied/missing resource convention, return
400 for malformed syntax, and use 409 for authorized replay payload conflicts and
invalid state transitions. A failed or unsealed run has no downloadable Report output.
No caller-supplied current-version fallback and no partial bytes on integrity failure.
After acceptance a later legitimate T24 supersession retains exact historical content
for the original report when its accepted reference remains eligible.

Use a short admission transaction to lock the scoped request, validate exact active
template/parameter/source and the Workflow action bound to its terminal instance,
mark the legacy request APPROVED with that instance, then insert a QUEUED run through
existing physical queue guards and bind the immutable action once. Persist RUNNING
while a separate bounded render transaction executes. Within that transaction, lock
the receipt, recheck current authorization and source, render deterministic bytes
(max 64 KiB for this profile), and create/upload one managed T24 DRAFT. Commit the
draft reference with the RENDERED lifecycle phase (legacy run stays RUNNING). For
recognized render/storage failure, roll back draft metadata and use a separate
short authorized transaction with a state compare to retain a terminal FAILED
code for the same run. Never record FAILED for a denied admission or substitute a
new run after replay. If the process stops before the render transaction commits,
the same request key may resume the same queued/running receipt under row
serialization and fresh authority. Committed renders, failed runs and sealed runs
replay without writing a second artifact. Track unknown storage outcomes through
existing Documents owner reconciliation.

At seal, use the exact stored draft/version/hash and independent native custodian.
Call the T24 acceptance operation and finish the existing output artifact and run
atomically. Store one `PRIMARY_REPORT` JSON output only on COMPLETED, with the
T24 acceptance ID, version and immutable checksum/length. Use row locks, uniqueness
and deferred owner consistency checks so duplicate or conflicting actions, stale
states, failures and rollback cannot manufacture a second success. Validate eligible
sealed content afresh with bounded verified bytes. Generic Reporting queue/artifact
aliases cannot operate on T25-owned request/run identities. For generated T24
documents, generic Documents pages omit managed output rows before pagination/count,
and direct aliases require current Reporting read in addition to normal Documents
authority. A marker in the Documents owner schema limits draft mutation and acceptance
to the Reporting owner contract using the existing transaction-bound guard pattern.
Preserve ordinary T24 document behavior. Record requester/reviewer/custodian, exact
scope, receipt IDs, template hash, source hash, Workflow action/instance and output
acceptance in durable evidence.

#### T25 acceptance and publication checks

1. **Primary signed journey.** Run one native LOCAL HTTP journey against a freshly
   migrated PostgreSQL 16 instance with disjoint requester, Workflow reviewer and
   custodian identities. Produce an exact T23 metric, submit a typed report, obtain
   an exact bound Workflow decision, render, seal through T24 and retrieve byte-for-byte

   Workflow action and exact T24 accepted version. Start a separate application
   OS-JVM over the same database/storage and read the original result again. Preserve
   original bytes after legitimate supersession and reject any “latest” substitution.
2. **Authorization and validation.** Deny anonymous/foreign facility or company,
   revoked paired grants, current policy denial, invalid template/parameter and
   failed or mismatched T23 inputs, reused/wrong Workflow target or self-review,
   same uploader/custodian, unsealed/failed output, and legacy alias attempts.
   Check protected detail, bytes and generic Documents discovery/count behavior.
   A corrupt/missing binary must not return part of an artifact.
3. **Integrity.** Test exact replay, changed-payload conflict, one winner under
   concurrent render/seal, transaction rollback after managed upload, durable
   terminal failed render with no accepted version/output, and no legacy or
   database-only successful state without same-scope owner evidence. Verify JDBC
   writes against the fresh Flyway/JPA baseline and keep all historical guards.
4. **CI and stop.** Use the existing required Java/architecture and 14 PostgreSQL
   lanes plus runtime OpenAPI compatibility/equality, strict physical dictionary
   equality and Full Verification Gate. Verify expected main, exact tree/paths,
   inventory cases and publication SHA. Observe matching workflow creation,
   queueing or startup and stop. T25 stays in progress after publication,
   with exact-SHA CI and signed synthetic acceptance required before completion.
