#### T26 scope and dependencies

**T26 — Execute and replay a governed synthetic exchange (FG-15/A15).**
The selected candidate scope is one inbound profile, `SYNTHETIC_DOCUMENT_DRAFT_V1`,
from a configured local SANDBOX integration system to a T24 controlled
Documents draft. T24 is complete and supplies the receiver transaction,
scope and idempotent create. T25 completion satisfies task order. No
operational asset or live connection is part of the synthetic fixture.

The existing Integration REST and application service register systems, open
job runs and record message metadata. `TargetModuleImportPort` only exposes
availability, and `NoopExternalConnectorGateway` supplies no receiving
execution. Existing mapping, job, message, inbound record, retry and dead
letter tables are reusable. HMR-014 allocates run numbers and forbids a
terminal run changing status. Each T26 attempt must therefore have its own
native run and message, with a stable scoped exchange ID across attempts.
T24 already binds a created draft to a facility and an idempotency key in
one transaction, so T26 requires a narrow Documents export and no new
Documents persistence model.

Integration owns the admitted mapping snapshot, exchange identity,
attempt sequence, controlled outcome and replay. Documents owns the
created draft. Identity owns live grant and policy evidence. Topology owns
the facility and company association. Use an Integration-side outbound
bridge for the three narrow owner contracts. No direct cross-owner writes
or foreign keys. The result is one draft receipt with its exact identifier.
Version upload, acceptance, external network calls, generic transformations,
SCADA, production data, schedules, webhooks and autonomous retries are outside
the scope.

#### T26 mapping, authorization and HTTP

The owner configures one active scope binding for the fixed profile and
its active manual inbound job definition, SANDBOX external system,
matching connector registry row, ACTIVE data contract and ACTIVE schema
version with STRICT mapping validation. Use existing catalog identifiers. The connector row
identifies configuration only. Validate the exact profile, lineage,
schema version and checksum, and the fixed allowlisted field mapping.
The one input field is bounded `titleFr` (1–160 characters, normalized
and checked for controls). The request also contains a bounded request
key and the selected profile ID and schema version ID. Freeze the
projection, map digest, source version, Documents type and classification
IDs, and approved scope before delivery. Documents validates those
catalog IDs at execution. The server derives the destination code and
idempotency key from the exchange ID. Store the bounded sanitized typed
projection and a SHA-256 digest. Reject arbitrary object fields, URLs,
unapproved payload modes and caller-supplied destination, actor or status.
A changed mapping or receiver configuration after admission must fail
closed for replay if it invalidates the pinned tuple. Prior evidence
remains readable under current authority.

Use current native LOCAL identity and paired direct grants at
`CUSTOM integration-company:{companyId}` and `FACILITY {facilityId}`.
Require an Identity policy PERMIT at both scopes and current Topology
ownership. Require Integration read before read projections and the
operation-specific grant on execute or replay. Replay additionally
requires a distinct currently authorized operator, a bounded reason,
and the expected failed attempt ordinal. Both sender and replayer must
satisfy Documents create scope when delivering under their own identity.
The Integration view omits unrelated Documents content. Any Documents
detail request uses the existing Documents read fence.

Base path `/api/v1/integration/companies/{companyId}/facilities/{facilityId}`.

| Method and suffix | Input, result and authority |
|---|---|
| GET `/synthetic-mappings/{profileId}` | Active pinned-profile candidate and schema version/checksum. Requires `integration:synthetic-exchange:read`. |
| POST `/synthetic-exchanges` | `T26SubmitExchange(requestKey, mappingProfileId, schemaVersionId, titleFr)`. Requires `integration:synthetic-exchange:execute` and read. Returns 201 on first admission, 200 on exact same-actor replay, with the logical exchange and first-attempt outcome. |
| GET `/synthetic-exchanges/{exchangeId}` | Scoped summary, pinned version/digests, latest attempt, safe dead-letter state and owner receipt only on success. Requires read. |
| GET `/synthetic-exchanges/{exchangeId}/attempts` | Bounded ordered history with attempt, actor, native run and message IDs, safe reason and timestamps. Requires read. |
| POST `/synthetic-exchanges/{exchangeId}/replay` | `T26ReplayExchange(requestKey, expectedAttempt, reason)`. Requires `integration:synthetic-exchange:replay` and read. Exact same reviewer/key returns the same replay outcome. Competing or stale eligible requests return 409. |

Use the existing protected unavailable policy before exposing existence,
history or counts. Malformed input returns 400, eligible digest or state
conflict returns 409, and transient receiver failure is a typed logged
outcome. Exclude raw exception text and sensitive payloads from receipts.

#### T26 transaction and state envelope

1. In a short admission transaction lock the scope/key, deduplicate exact
   payload and actor, and persist the scoped exchange and immutable
   mapping snapshot. Claim attempt 1 with one allocated HMR-014 run, one
   synthetic exchange message and one inbound record. Preserve separate
   receipt linkage for each attempt and require one current attempt per exchange.
2. In a separate bounded transaction lock the exchange and attempt,
   recheck current authority and the admitted configuration, call the
   Documents contract and persist the receiver ID and all success states
   atomically. Store that ID only on success. No receiver commit is
   possible independently of the Integration success receipt. Use
   the existing T24 request key and scoped Documents creation semantics.
3. A recognized transient database/receiver failure rolls back the
   receiving transaction. A new short transaction fences the same
   attempt and commits its terminal failure and a single OPEN dead letter.
   Do not produce a dead letter for denied admission or misclassify unknown
   commits. Resolve ambiguous outcomes by re-reading the durable exchange
   before resumption. Keep a bounded attempt lease. On expired interrupted
   claims, use the same fenced attempt for original same-actor resumption,
   or mark it ABANDONED under privileged replay when no result committed.
   Never allow an expired claimant to write success after another claim.
4. Permit one manual replay for a retryable dead letter or a fenced abandoned
   first claim. Serialize replay admission on the exchange. Allocate a new
   native job/message/inbound record, retain the first terminal states, and
   keep the same Documents idempotency key. A replay success sets the dead
   letter REPLAYED with actual actor/reason/time and one receiving outcome.
   Second failure remains a terminal dead letter, with both attempt facts
   intact. No implicit retry or silent state rewrite.
5. The migration adds an Integration-owned scoped mapping binding, exchange
   receipt and attempt receipt. Pin exact local parent pairs, enforce unique
   scope/idempotency and ordinals, constrain phase/receipt shape, retain
   terminal evidence and test deferred guards at real commit. Reserve the
   profile from legacy Integration start/message writes and reject orphan
   writes on reserved keys at the physical boundary. Provision only three
   permission identities. Supply owner configuration and grants in synthetic
   fixtures. Preserve all prior migrations and native owner constraints.

#### T27 scope and dependencies

**T27 — Deliver a recipient-scoped notification inbox (FG-16 / A16).**
Use one event, `WORKFLOW_REPORT_REVIEW_TASK_ASSIGNED_V1`, and one channel,
`WEB`. Workflow owns task assignment and status. Reporting owns the
request and its company/facility locator. Notification owns inbox delivery
and acknowledgement. Identity owns live grants and actor identity. Topology
owns current facility-to-company linkage. The WEB delivery receipt means
the item was durably made available in HidraAPI. The existing local async
gateway accepts provider requests and supplies no proof of WEB delivery
or receipt. Existing legacy Notification entities and ingress endpoints
remain separate from this protected slice.

**Source event.** Hook the existing native Workflow task creation use case
after a validated task save. Require a current ACTIVE Workflow definition
with code `T27_SCOPED_REPORT_APPROVAL_INBOX_V1` and matching running version,
an exact active `reporting / REPORT_REQUEST / REPORT_APPROVAL` binding,
and a new OPEN task directly assigned to one eligible actor other than the
instance starter. Resolve the current step's `defaultAssignmentRuleId` through the existing
rule repository. Require an active rule for the same definition and step
and the same actor; resolve `DIRECT` through the active assignment-mode
catalog. The persisted task may omit its optional assignment-mode ID,
but a supplied mode must also resolve to DIRECT. Exclude role,
organization pool and target owner indirection. Existing validation and configured authorization remain
in force. Only the corresponding Reporting owner callback can translate
the admitted target into an inbox command. Default callback denies for an
opted-in flow with unavailable ownership resolution. Ordinary Workflow
definitions and unselected assignment forms produce no T27 event.

Use the existing Reporting owner access check in the original transaction.
Resolve the exact T25 request and fixed scope from the Reporting repository,
require its current SUBMITTED phase and a current authorized request
starter, and pass only task ID, persisted audience actor, scope and the
assignment timestamp to Notification. The callback and Notification export
join the original transaction with MANDATORY propagation. A failed insert
rolls back the task and inbox write together. Notification cannot call back
into Workflow for acknowledgement. No generated events from older tasks,
new workflow definition seeds, provider delivery, external transport,
free-text rendering, or background dispatch enter this slice.

**Notification state and persistence.** Create one immutable WEB item per
admitted Workflow task. Event identity is the fixed event type plus the
persisted Workflow task ID, never a client key. Duplicate internal delivery
with the exact same scope, recipient and assignment timestamp returns the
stable item. A conflicting replay fails the caller transaction. Reuse the
existing domain enums for `WEB` and acknowledgement status where applicable.
Mint a server UUID for the item. Store fixed event code, company and facility
IDs, recipient actor ID, Workflow task ID, and assigned/delivered timestamps.
Expose a fixed safe message code. An inbox item has `DELIVERED` delivery and
`REQUIRED` acknowledgement until the single durable acknowledgement exists.
That insert derives the actor from current authority; repeated or concurrent
acknowledgements return the originally committed timestamp. It does not
update the item, Workflow task, Workflow instance, or approval evidence.

Add `public.hidra_notification_t27_inbox_item` and
`public.hidra_notification_t27_inbox_acknowledgement`. For the item require
nonblank, bounded owner identifiers, fixed event/channel, correct timestamp
ordering, and unique event identity. Add a descending index on company,
facility, recipient, delivered timestamp and UUID for keyset scans.
Acknowledgement has one row per item and a local composite FK binding item
ID and original recipient actor. Require the DB acknowledgement timestamp
to be at or after delivery under that item lock. Block UPDATE, DELETE and
TRUNCATE on both tables. Store external owner identifiers as scalars with no
cross-owner FKs. Use PostgreSQL insert-on-conflict and a scoped reread that
compares the original immutable fields. Unexpected persistence failures stay
server errors.

#### T27 REST and access contract

Base path `/api/v1/notification/companies/{companyId}/facilities/{facilityId}`.

| Operation | Exact controller method signature | Contract |
|---|---|---|
| GET `/inbox` | `list(String companyId, String facilityId, Integer limit, String cursor)` | Operation ID `listT27NotificationInbox`. Default 25, max 100, descending `(deliveredAt,id)`, exclusive cursor, fetch at most limit + 1. Return `items` and optional `nextCursor` with no counts. |
| GET `/inbox/{notificationId}` | `detail(String companyId, String facilityId, String notificationId)` | Operation ID `readT27NotificationInboxItem`. Return the recipient's current delivery and acknowledgement state. |
| POST `/inbox/{notificationId}/acknowledgement` | `acknowledge(String companyId, String facilityId, String notificationId)` | Operation ID `acknowledgeT27NotificationInboxItem`. Bodyless and idempotent. Return HTTP 200 and the same acknowledgement receipt on retry. |

Use explicit DTOs with unique T27 schema names. Allow only notification UUID,
event/message codes, WEB channel, delivery status, delivered timestamp,
acknowledgement status and optional acknowledged timestamp. No report or
Workflow identifiers, recipient PII, user-supplied content or provider
references are returned. No client recipient selector, list-wide totals,
provider diagnostics or legacy list aliases. Encode the cursor as bounded
base64url of a versioned delivered-time/UUID tuple, validate syntax and
precision and use it only as a SQL boundary after access checks.

All routes require `notification:inbox:read`. The POST also requires
`notification:inbox:acknowledge`. Seed only those permission identities,
with no grants. Identity must recheck the exact signed, current native LOCAL
session, explicit current direct permits for CUSTOM
`notification-company:<companyId>` and FACILITY `<facilityId>`, and
deny-precedence under the same transaction. Reuse the current Identity ports
and evaluator. Topology must confirm current active facility ownership in
that company. Resolve authority before any inbox query and include company,
facility and authenticated recipient in every read, row lock and write.
Unauthenticated callers use existing authentication errors. Authenticated
out-of-scope or unknown item IDs share a non-disclosing not-found response.
An authorized foreign recipient with an empty inbox sees an empty list.
Existing report/action endpoints continue to apply their own owner and
Workflow authority. Inbox grants confer no Workflow permissions.

#### T28 ownership and source event

**T28 — Search and export scoped Audit evidence (FG-17 / A17).**
Deliver one end-to-end slice for T22 governed Risk approval evidence,
using the existing `RISK_ASSESSMENT_APPROVED` Audit taxonomy, one current
company/facility pair, one explicit time range, and one export format.
Risk owns qualification, approval and the source scope. Audit owns scope
bindings, scoped event reads, exported bytes, manifests and access receipts.
Identity owns current actor and grants. Topology owns current facility-to-company
linkage. Audit stores the bounded immutable artifact in PostgreSQL under its
own authority. There is no Documents dependency for this slice.

The existing Audit ledger does not contain an authoritative company/facility
pair. Populate an Audit-owned, append-only binding in the original T22
approval transaction. Extend `RiskAssessmentAuditContract.ApprovalEvidence`
with an optional typed `ApprovalScope(companyId, facilityId)` and retain the
old constructor for legacy callers. Only the governed Risk branch forwards
the exact scope already established by its locked owner proof and current
approval authorization. The legacy approval branch still appends its
normal event without a T28 binding. The existing Audit adapter writes the
ordinary event through `RecordAuditEventUseCase` and binds its exact flushed
event ID using an Audit-owned port. Require an active transaction for
scoped publication before writing the event. Failure to write either part
rolls back Audit, Risk and the Workflow decision in that transaction.
The binding uses an Audit-local FK to the immutable Audit event, unique
event ID and unique Workflow action identity. Enforce event type, exact
Risk source/target/action, matching action ID and occurred time at insertion.
Risk scope fields are owner-provided scalars. There is no cross-owner FK,
legacy backfill, payload parsing for scope, or public binding endpoint.
Legacy Audit APIs and existing business actions retain their behavior.

#### T28 REST, state and authorization

Base path `/api/v1/audit/companies/{companyId}/facilities/{facilityId}`.

| Method and path | Exact controller signature | Contract |
|---|---|---|
| GET `/events` | `search(String companyId, String facilityId, String eventType, Instant from, Instant to, Integer limit, String cursor)` | Operation ID `searchT28AuditEvents`. Typed event page. Default 25 and maximum 100 rows per page. |
| POST `/exports` | `createExport(String companyId, String facilityId, T28CreateAuditExport request)` | Operation ID `createT28AuditExport`. Request contains request key, fixed purpose `GZ2_SYNTHETIC_ASSURANCE`, event type, from and to. Returns 201 on creation and 200 on exact replay with the same export and manifest. |
| GET `/exports/{exportId}` | `exportManifest(String companyId, String facilityId, UUID exportId)` | Operation ID `readT28AuditExportManifest`. Return `COMPLETED` plus stored manifest, never bytes on this route. |
| GET `/exports/{exportId}/content` | `download(String companyId, String facilityId, UUID exportId)` | Operation ID `downloadT28AuditExportContent`. Return exact bounded JSON bytes as an attachment after current authorization and committed access evidence. |

Require the explicit event type `RISK_ASSESSMENT_APPROVED` and UTC instants
with at most microsecond precision. Use a half-open interval `[from,to)`
with positive duration capped at 31 days. Validate bounded nonblank owner
identifiers, a request key of 1–80 characters and a bounded base64url,
versioned cursor. Cursor contains only the descending `(occurredAt,eventId)`
boundary. Apply predicates for company, facility, type and time before
ordering, paging or export. Scan at most limit + 1 rows for search and at
most 1,001 rows for export. An admitted scope with no events returns an
empty page or a zero-event export. The safe event projection contains
only event ID, event type, operation, target ID, Workflow action ID and
occurred time. Exclude Audit payloads, access records, internal exception
text, names, usernames, request metadata and free text.

All four operations require `audit:scoped-evidence:read`. Export creation,
manifest and content also require `audit:scoped-evidence:export`. Seed
only the two permission identities, with no assigned grants. Recheck
the persisted binding and current security state of the signed native
LOCAL actor. Require current direct permits for both CUSTOM
`audit-company:<companyId>` and FACILITY `<facilityId>` for each required
permission, with deny precedence. Confirm the active facility's exact
company with the existing locked Topology owner proof. Use regular
transactions, including reads, for Identity and Topology locks. Bind
export reads and downloads to the originating actor and exact scope.
An authenticated caller receives the same non-disclosing 404 for unknown
and out-of-scope export identities. Authenticate before any protected
query. Return 400 for invalid typed inputs, 409 for a valid changed request
under the same key, 422 for export size limits, and a safe unavailable
response on integrity or access-evidence persistence failures. Use the
existing platform authentication behavior for invalid or missing sessions.

Create a frozen export synchronously. Serialize admission per
`(company,facility,requester,requestKey)` with a transaction-scoped advisory
lock and enforce the same tuple with a unique constraint. Use one
scope-filtered SELECT for the ordered snapshot. Encode a fixed
`GZ2_AUDIT_EVIDENCE_JSON_V1` document with stable field order, fixed UTC
timestamp representation, UTF-8 and one final newline. Check a 1,000-row,
262,144-byte cap. Persist the exact bytes, event count, length, SHA-256,
normalized criteria, fixed purpose, requester, receipt ID and completion
time atomically with successful request-access evidence. The manifest
identifies the format, scope, criteria, byte length, digest and count.
Exact retry returns original bytes/manifest identity even after new events
are appended. A failed or oversized request persists no partial export.
Download checks stored length and recomputed SHA-256 before returning
bytes. Send `application/json`, a server-generated attachment filename,
content length, `Content-Digest` with the base64-encoded SHA-256 and
`Cache-Control: no-store`.

For download, authenticate the native actor separately from business
authorization in the same transaction. Represent expected scope and
permission denial as values through the Identity/Topology bridges. Avoid
throwing across transactional boundaries for ordinary denials. Commit an
append-only access receipt before producing the HTTP result. Allow receipts
carry the verified scoped export reference and current actor. For denied
requests by valid native actors, record actor, UTC time, action, outcome
and a digest of the normalized requested scope/export locator. Do not fetch
or persist a protected export reference on pre-query denial. For an admitted
lookup with no matching export, record the same denial shape. A corrupt
artifact yields a committed integrity-failure receipt without bytes. If
evidence cannot commit, return an unavailable error without bytes. Never
log raw credentials, export payload, or exception content. This receipt
records the authorization outcome of handing bytes to the HTTP layer.

Use three Audit-owned relations `hidra_audit_t28_event_scope`,
`hidra_audit_t28_export`, and `hidra_audit_t28_access_receipt` in `public`.
Enforce scoped composite keys and local FKs, fixed value and timestamp
constraints, byte/count limits, SHA-256 consistency, access-outcome reference
rules, and UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE guards on all three. Index
`(company_id,facility_id,event_type,occurred_at DESC,event_id DESC)`.
Use database constraints and same-owner checks to preserve immutable
evidence and scope. Neither a provider, a background export worker, nor
an operational retention/deployment policy is needed for A17.

#### T28 complete acceptance checklist and publication

Use the existing signed T22 journey on a fresh fully migrated PostgreSQL 16
database and advance it through the real owner REST approval and T28 HTTP
entry points. The following assertions constitute the complete A17 acceptance
scope and must run in enrolled CI.

1. **Source and transaction.** Force a test-only scope-binding insert failure
   during real final approval. Assert no committed Audit event or scope
   binding, Risk approval or Workflow decision. Retry through the native
   entry point and prove exact event, action, facility and company lineage.
2. **Selection.** Produce genuine Risk approvals for the selected facility,
   another facility of the same company, and a facility of a second company.
   Seed additional facility configuration only in the signed fixture. Use
   captured event timestamps to prove both half-open boundaries, inclusive
   lower bound and exclusive upper bound. Include a legacy unbound Audit event
   of matching type as a negative control. Assert the exact event ID sets in
   search results and artifact bytes, pagination without duplicates or leakage,
   and an admitted empty search/export. Cover invalid or oversized criteria.
3. **Export integrity.** Race two exact create retries. Require one 201 and
   one 200, one durable export ID, equal manifests and no duplicate artifact.
   Verify changed criteria on the same key return 409. Recompute SHA-256 over
   the exact download bytes, verify lengths, row ordering and attachment
   headers, then reread the same bytes after a new qualifying event and one
   application process restart. At the end of the same enrolled case, bulk-insert
   synthetic Audit-owned event/binding rows with valid identifiers into an isolated
   time window solely to exercise both caps. Make one window exceed 1,000 rows
   and a separate window stay within 1,000 rows while exceeding 262,144 serialized
   bytes. Verify 422 and no export or success receipt for either request. Do not
   use the bulk fixtures to establish native owner-event admission.
4. **Current authority.** Use signed read-only, other-requester, mismatched
   company/facility and revoked callers. Assert no manifest or bytes for
   out-of-scope or unknown exports. Revoke a facility export grant while the
   original JWT is still valid, then assert download denial and a committed,
   actor-bound denial receipt with no protected export reference. Preserve
   permission-deny precedence. Assert each admitted download has a distinct
   committed access receipt. Inject an access-evidence write failure and
   assert no bytes leave the API, then remove the fault and verify retry.
5. **Physical and compatibility.** Reject direct mutation of scoped bindings,
   artifacts and access receipts, plus inconsistent scope/reference and byte
   hash writes. Preserve the original T22 assertions and enrolled compatibility
   coverage. The same Full Verification Gate requires static and architecture,
   all 14 PostgreSQL shards, backward compatibility, canonical runtime OpenAPI
   equality and strict physical dictionary equality.

The confirmed residual implementation scope is HSE. The native case and CAPA
lists currently accept only page/size. HSE case list calculates a
company/facility total before proving current Incident access for each
returned row. A row outside that page can therefore contribute to a total
without going through the owner check. The legacy JPA queries exclude
enrolled case/CAPA rows, but legacy detail currently distinguishes an
enrolled identifier (404) from an absent valid identifier (400).
The configurable generic Workbench uses metamodel-derived HSE entity
resources and has no HSE prohibition in its exposure policy. Its default
configuration is empty. Explicitly prevent generic exposure of the scoped
case data and dependent evidence, without changing the legacy policy for
non-enrolled records that have no reliable company/facility binding.
No inferred scope, historical backfill, or new permission identity.

#### T29 bounded contract

- Extend existing `discoverScopedHseCases` at
  `GET /api/v1/hse/companies/{companyId}/facilities/{facilityId}/cases`
  with optional `caseNumber`, and existing `listScopedHseCapas` at
  `GET /api/v1/hse/companies/{companyId}/facilities/{facilityId}/cases/{caseId}/capas`
  with optional `actionNumber`. Use exact case-sensitive comparison after
  the same trim/80-character bound as the write use cases. An explicitly
  blank or oversized key is 400 after scope authorization. Preserve the
  default page size, size cap, response DTOs, operation IDs and verbs.
  Existing case/action numbers are not a uniqueness constraint. Return
  all admitted exact matches in the existing deterministic order with ID
  tie-breakers; an absent filter is the existing discovery contract.
- Keep current HSE grants, facility ownership and reviewed Incident
  proof as prerequisites. HSE case discovery must authorize every match
  contributing to the count, including off-page rows, using the established
  Incident owner contract in the same transaction. Preserve fail-closed
  unavailable behavior if matching Incident evidence cannot be admitted;
  emit no page or count. Unexpected persistence/owner failures remain
  errors. Perform scope and key filtering in SQL and use a single ordered
  candidate snapshot, processing in bounded fetch batches and retaining
  only the requested page. Derive both count and page from that same
  candidate set. Avoid separate count then page queries, unbounded
  buffering and cross-module SQL. CAPA list first proves the exact parent
  and its Incident authorization, then applies exact key and parent
  criteria identically to data and totals in one statement snapshot,
  including empty or out-of-range pages. Keep existing detail and history
  projections.
- Authorized no-match collection is 200 with empty items and zero total.
  An authorized page beyond the last match has empty items and the valid
  filtered total. Denied HSE scope or revoked grant uses the existing
  scope denial; unavailable exact objects and failed Incident proof use
  the same non-disclosing 404 contract as other unavailable HSE resources.
  Never disclose foreign scope, protected IDs, keys, rows or totals in
  denials. Legacy direct detail uses the same generic 404 for both an
  enrolled and absent well-formed ID, preserving 400 for malformed input
  and existing typed successful legacy responses.
- Generic Workbench denies HSE persistence resources for cases, corrective
  preventive actions, case status histories, case evidence links, impact
  assessments and closures at configuration and runtime exposure checks.
  Use the exact existing metamodel-derived keys and cover both Workbench
  route aliases by their shared policy. Preserve unrelated resources.
  HSE owns read criteria and projections; Identity and Incident retain
  current authority and reviewed source checks through existing ports.

#### T31 goal, dependencies and ownership

T07 is COMPLETED and provides exact published baseline read by company,
pipeline and receipt ID, with current scope, historical pin authorization,
and original protected transaction verification. The existing T15 signed
GZ2 test publishes, supersedes and reconstructs that baseline across a
JVM restart. Reuse that journey for A19. The legacy Simulation scenario
create path stores a model version and generic topology snapshot selector;
run admission expects a legacy LOCKED scenario. Those contracts do not
supply the T31 immutable baseline-pinned revision lifecycle.

Simulation owns the scenario and its revisions, validation rules and
capability truth. Topology owns the baseline receipt, epoch, manifest and
canonical digest. Identity owns the current signed LOCAL actor and grants.
Use synthetic gas inputs on the existing GZ2 baseline. T31 is an input
preparation contract with declared engineering units and a versioned
structural check. Existing simulation tables and legacy REST behavior
remain intact. Numerical execution, network-node mapping, hydraulic
adequacy, calibration, engine selection, results, operational actions,
and third-party integration belong outside this stage.

#### Native API and behavior

Base path `/api/v1/simulation/companies/{companyId}/pipeline-systems/{pipelineSystemId}/scenarios`.

| Verb and relative path | Operation ID | Behavior |
|---|---|---|
| POST base | `createT31Scenario` | Create revision 1 and return 201. Exact authorized replay returns 200 with the original revision. |
| POST `/{scenarioId}/revisions` | `appendT31ScenarioRevision` | Accept a full replacement input set with required positive `expectedRevision`. Append the next immutable revision or return 409 for stale head or key conflict. Exact authorized replay returns 200, including after later revisions. |
| GET `/{scenarioId}/revisions/{revision}` | `readT31ScenarioRevision` | Read one exact version with baseline and input provenance. An unavailable revision uses the protected 404 contract. |
| GET `/{scenarioId}/revisions/{revision}/validation` | `validateT31ScenarioRevision` | Recompute the deterministic structural validation from exact persisted inputs and its recorded policy version, without mutating rows. Return ordered diagnostic codes and truthful capability. |

The typed write input carries an exact baseline receipt UUID and lowercase
64-character expected manifest digest, a bounded scenario name (1–120
trimmed characters), intended mode `STEADY` or `TRANSIENT`, a request key
(1–80 trimmed characters), and explicit boundary values. For this first
profile use the declared slots `SUPPLY_PRESSURE` (absolute `PA` or
`BAR_ABSOLUTE`) and `DELIVERY_MASS_FLOW` (`KG_PER_S`). These slots
identify scenario inputs, not resolved network nodes. Store the submitted
decimal value and unit, with bounded precision (18 digits, at most 6
fractional digits), as well as the exact SI representation in typed reads.
Pressure must be positive and delivery flow nonnegative. STEADY has no
time controls. TRANSIENT uses required positive integer duration and
step in seconds, step divides duration and there are at most 10,000
intervals. Both declared boundary values are constant over that window.
Malformed, mixed-mode and incompatible input returns a bounded 400
response after route admission as applicable. Choose and freeze a
documented canonical digest encoding and validation policy ID
`T31_INPUT_V1`. Use locale-independent decimal normalization and bind
mode, declared values/units, baseline reference and actual owner digest
into the input digest. No implicit default unit or current baseline
fallback. A valid revision reports `VALIDATED_INPUTS` and
`numericalCapability=NOT_AVAILABLE` for both modes. It carries no
result values, solver job or operational qualification.

Require paired direct current grants for company
(`CUSTOM simulation-company:{companyId}`) and exact `PIPELINE_SYSTEM`.
`simulation:scenario-inputs:read` governs both reads and
`simulation:scenario-inputs:write` is additionally required for both
writes. Reuse Identity's signed LOCAL actor, direct-grant evidence,
deny-precedence evaluator and original-transaction grant checks.
The new permissions start ungranted. Establish authorized Simulation
scope before looking up scenario history or invoking Topology. For each
operation, use the narrow Topology export to execute its existing T07 EXACT
read with the same principal, company/pipeline and receipt; compare the
owner digest and never resolve `current`. Keep Topology's protected
executor in its own original transaction, outside a Simulation
transaction. Use the proof only for that request and only for immutable
receipt facts. Recheck Simulation grants in the transaction that
loads or writes the final scoped revision. For reads, obtain only the
scoped baseline locator in the initial transaction and confirm the same
locator on final read. These are two owner authorization decisions, with
no claim of cross-transaction atomic revocation. No scenario write goes
ahead after a failed Topology decision. Missing/foreign baseline,
missing scenario/revision and denied source pins must not disclose
existence or facts. Fail unexpected owner/database errors as service
failures without returning protected data. Topology continues to enforce
current historical source rights even after supersession.

One Simulation-owned append-only table with `(scenario_id, revision)`
key stores immutable scope, prior revision, exact baseline tuple, inputs,
actor/time, policy/version, digest and replay key/fingerprint. Enforce
positive contiguous predecessor and immutable scope using a same-owner
predecessor FK and check, including no predecessor on revision 1. Use
unique scoped actor/request key and revision slots to arbitrate concurrent
commands. Preserve exact replay only for identical canonical operations,
including target and expected revision where applicable. Re-read the
committed winner when concurrent requests collide; different commands
must not rewrite or silently replace history. Reject direct UPDATE,
DELETE and TRUNCATE with immutable database guards. There is no FK to
Topology-owned private persistence, and no new ORM entity.

#### Proposed behavior within the existing Configuration boundary

Retire one existing B5 PUBLIC/INTERNAL typed environment override by
appending an immutable cutoff receipt. Identify it by value ID and verify
the exact definition ID, active definition version and environment. Preserve
the original value row, status, audit fields and definition version. The
existing effective reader uses the earlier of the original exclusive end
and retirement cutoff. Immediately before cutoff it returns the original
value and provenance. At and after cutoff it returns the admitted successor
if one is effective, otherwise the existing typed default, with the
existing source indicator. A successor may begin exactly at the cutoff.
Restrict cutoffs to microsecond-aligned future instants inside the original
window at transaction time. Preserve current authority, redaction, typed
default, and legacy exclusions. Feature flags, whole-definition
retirement, secrets, arbitrary scopes and other modules are outside this
envelope.

Add `POST /api/v1/configuration/values/{valueId}/retirement-preview`
(read-only, HTTP 200) and `PUT /api/v1/configuration/values/{valueId}/retirement`
(HTTP 201, exact authorized replay HTTP 200). Preview accepts definition ID,
definition version ID, environment and cutoff. It returns server-derived
before/after source and value IDs without raw payloads or secret references,
plus a server-computed state token binding the target, cutoff and resolved
transition (including the successor at cutoff or the default version).
Commit uses the same fields plus the token. Recompute under the existing
definition lock, record actor from the bearer, and recheck current
authority before returning or committing. Verify current authority first
on replay, then return the original receipt for the same actor and exact
request even after the cutoff. Reject changed or stale tokens, competing
retirements, and unsupported lifecycle states with 409, invalid fields
with 400, authority failure with 403 (401 for unauthenticated requests),
and authorized unknown or mismatched targets with the same 404. Preview
does not promise that future authorized writes cannot change the post-cutoff
resolution.

#### T33 approved meaning and source-backed boundaries

- **Authority = current Identity permission AND effective Organization responsibility AND exact current Topology relationship.** Each is independently required. An explicit Identity DENY at an applicable exact/ancestor scope takes precedence; any INDETERMINATE, missing owner, stale identity, unavailable provider, ambiguous owner relationship or failed current verification denies. No actor/user/employee ID supplied by the browser is authority. Employee number, username similarity, job title, region display name, OrganizationUnit membership or geographic proximity never grant an operation on their own.
- Identity resolves the native authenticated current ACTIVE, unlocked User and its `employeeReferenceId`. Organization must establish the same ACTIVE employee, reciprocal `identityUserReference` when populated, current effective responsibility (`validFrom <= now < validTo`, `ACTIVE`) and, when using a unit-held responsibility, a distinct current employee-to-unit assignment plus the unit's own effective status. A unit appointment or direct employee responsibility is a **constraint**, not a permission grant; historical assignments remain immutable historical evidence. At most the existing `OWNER`, `ACCOUNTABLE` and `RESPONSIBLE` responsibilities can qualify this read; `SUPPORT`, `ESCALATION` and `APPROVER` do not become general regional reader rights.
- Existing Organization `OperationalScopeType` supports `GLOBAL`, `ORGANIZATION_UNIT`, `PIPELINE_SYSTEM`, `PIPELINE`, `FACILITY`, `EQUIPMENT`; there is **no** registered `PIPELINE_SECTION`. A selected section is the existing Topology pipeline segment, inheriting only through its verified owner pipeline relation; T33 must not create a fabricated registry type or infer a new section aggregate. `GLOBAL` and `ORGANIZATION_UNIT` responsibility alone are insufficient to expand physical rights. An exact equipment responsibility covers that equipment only.
- Only Topology may resolve authoritative pipeline-to-system, segment-to-pipeline, facility-to-system through effective `PipelineSystemFacility`, and equipment-to-facility or segment. Parent scope may flow downward solely along a verified active association at the evaluation instant. No upward, sibling or transitive cross-system propagation. Conflicting direct facility/segment bindings, mixed-company or multiply associated shared assets fail closed unless separately and exactly authorized for the selected company and asset. Historical engineering draft metadata and display labels are not company authority. Company context must be checked against a live, owner-qualified company/system association; the presence of a draft, publication copy, `companyPartyId` string or map geometry alone does not prove company ownership.
- Cross-region and foreign-company requested resource identity, coordinates, metadata, geometry, existence, counts, histories and graph neighborhood must not be disclosed. The G1 decision is current-request-only and never a durable authorization token. Any required backend permission (including one for the dedicated query route) is checked at request time; existing route permission, legacy administrator paths and protected owner operations are not globally relaxed. Synthetic GZ2 identities and scopes are test data, not installed OT or legal region catalog entries.
- **No new table/migration is admitted** for this read-only authorization composition. Use the current Identity/Organization/Topology owners and existing persistence relationships. If an authoritative company association cannot be proved by current source, the safe outcome is unavailable/deny, not a guessed association or an unapproved schema extension.

#### T33 API, domain, ports and implementation contract

The one admitted typed, authenticated, non-mutating client query is
`GET /api/v1/identity/me/regional-access/{resourceKind}/{resourceId}?companyPartyId=...`.
`resourceKind` accepts exactly `PIPELINE_SYSTEM`, `PIPELINE`, `PIPELINE_SEGMENT`, `FACILITY`, `EQUIPMENT`.
`companyPartyId` is an untrusted selector and must be verified against the Topology owner, not inferred as an access grant. A successfully permitted exact resource returns only its kind/id, selected company and `permitted=true` (no inherited foreign objects or grant details). Missing authentication is 401, missing route permission is 403, and resource absent versus forbidden/foreign is non-disclosing 404. Owner unavailability fails closed without revealing the requested protected identity. The URI is a **target API** until the new runtime OpenAPI is generated and accepted; do not assert it exists today.

Identity owns a pure-Java policy combining three owner decisions; a typed inbound use case obtains the server-side actor, evaluates current Identity grant/deny with the existing evaluator and current signed native binding, acquires effective Organization facts and Topology ancestry only through deliberate public contracts, and refuses unproved authority. Organization exports eligible employee/responsibility scalar snapshots, not private aggregates. Topology exports owner-resolved typed ancestry and company-context evidence, not JPA entities, map features or inferred edges. The REST adapter maps explicit DTOs and canonical error semantics. No general platform authorization bypass, foreign persistence access, generic Workbench exposure or cross-module domain import is admitted. Cross-module architecture exceptions must be exact, not package wildcards. T34 must reuse the completed T33 evaluator within each authorized map/discovery query; T33 alone does not retrofit map endpoint security.

#### T34 route and projection contract

All six operations are GET under `/api/v1/topology/regional-map` and
require an exact `companyPartyId` selector. The ordinary route gate
requires `topology:regional-map:read` for the five read operations and
`topology:regional-map:search` for search as derived by
`HidraRoutePermissionNaming`. Fixture grants for these route codes and
T33 resource grants are separate. A route grant gives no resource rights.
Use the signed current employee via T33. A company selector, client
region, previously returned feature or cached result gives no authority.
No trusted-native bypass registration, fallback to the global map,
or browser-callable permission override is admitted.

| Relative path | Outcome |
|---|---|
| `/layers` | Return the fixed supported layer descriptors with regional feature URLs. Descriptors expose no company inventory or grant data. |
| `/layers/{layerId}` | Resolve the descriptor from the same fixed catalog. Unknown layer returns 404. |
| `/layers/{layerId}/features` | Return one authorized layer as a typed paginated FeatureCollection. Optional `q` filters visible fields. |
| `/layers/{layerId}/features/{entityId}` | Resolve an exact canonical ID within the specified layer and apply the identical projection policy. Unknown, geometry unavailable, foreign and denied features share 404. |
| `/geojson` | Return a FeatureCollection for the requested comma-delimited subset of layers (all six by default). Deduplicate layer IDs before aggregation. |
| `/search` | Search authorized scalar identifiers, codes and display names across the same projection. Return the existing typed search result. Require nonblank `q`. |

Require a canonical company selector and bound query length to 120
characters and page size to 1–500 (default 100, zero-based page default
0). Reject malformed selectors, query or pagination with 400. Use
deterministic layer order and entity-ID order within each layer, and
apply the same rules for totals, total pages and hasNext. Retain 401 for
unauthenticated and 403 for missing route authority. Collection queries
with no visible matching data return 200 with zero totals and no resource
metadata. Never redirect to a legacy endpoint or return a resource or
policy diagnostic. Return protected responses with private, no-store caching.

- For systems, pipelines, segments and facilities, call the existing
  `TopologyRegionalAccessContract` with that exact kind, ID and company.
  Use current active Topology rows, T33 canonical ancestry and effective
  facility linking. No upward or sibling grant. A system or pipeline
  feature needs its own permit and at least one visible drawable segment.
  Build MultiLineString only from visible child segments, and suppress
  parent ID properties unless independently permitted.
- A node has no independent T33 kind. Admit an active node with coordinates
  through a permitted active incident segment and, if it is tied to a
  facility, a separate exact facility permit. Establish permitted segment
  scope before node derivation, then require two admitted endpoints for
  drawing that segment. Display no hidden incident IDs, counts or neighbors.
  Use existing coordinate order and preserve individual segment lines.
- A connection needs an active row, a non-null permitted backing segment,
  and endpoints matching that segment in either order. Both nodes must
  be admitted. Preserve the connection's stored endpoint ordering and
  type. Missing, contradictory or cross-scope relationships are omitted.
  Never join visible fragments across an excluded edge.
- The owner query fetches company-qualified candidate IDs and scalar
  relationship references in deterministic bounded batches. Apply T33
  decisions before hydrating output metadata/coordinates and building
  geometry, matching search, counting or taking a public page. A page
  size limits emitted features and cannot limit the authorized total.
  Reuse exact decisions only within one request. Re-read contributing
  authority before emitting the completed projection and fail closed if
  it changed. Keep the enclosing transaction compatible with T33's
  transactional calls. Avoid per-layer global entity scans and state
  shared across requests.

or dossier payload across requests. All successful responses use

Run the existing protected executor outside any new dossier transaction and recheck selected pipeline/system scope and relationship after it returns. ### Owner decision: activate T36 with a configurable engineering authority contract — 2026-11-21

**Decision and prerequisite resolution.** The owner approved the T36 read-only
Topology pressure-restriction approach and clarified that identifying a named
SONATRACH department, individual approver or operational role assignment is
**not** a development prerequisite. For T36, “owning engineering authority”
means a **logical, company-scoped and resource-scoped engineering restriction
approval capability** whose authenticated grant, independence, decision and
Audit binding will be exercised by the later governed T38 write workflow.
The organization maps that capability to its authorized personnel at deployment.
No SONATRACH-specific department is embedded in the domain model, schema,
controller, permissions or test fixtures.

**Selected class and ownership.** Admit exactly the first-class **upper operating
pressure restriction**, on an exact pipeline or exact section, for an approved
condition and half-open effective interval. Topology owns the immutable read
projection, resolution and REST contract; Identity owns current actor and
resource scope; T07 provides separately protected published-baseline
provenance; Workflow and Audit own authorized decision and immutable evidence
contracts. A T07 approval qualifies its engineering baseline **only**: it is
not a restriction approval. Integrity owns contributing assessments but no
Integrity-derived operating limit is admitted until separately authorized.
Design pressure and manufacturer equipment information are never promoted
into operating limits by inference.

**Qualification/decision rule.** A QUALIFIED T36 read requires a complete,
immutable, internally consistent and separately authorized restriction-revision
qualification binding to an exact published T07 receipt/digest, the admitted
engineering source revision, an independent approval decision and immutable
Audit reference, with the declared company, target, unit and pressure basis.
A bare decision UUID, role name, asserted `approved` flag, unqualified
assessment or client-supplied declaration is insufficient. The projection
must be read-only for the application role, with no writer, runtime seeder or
live operational restriction data. Synthetic fixtures may exercise qualified
approval witnesses only when their tests prove the evidence contract and
fail-closed rejection paths; they are not operationally approved records.
Until an admissible independently authorized decision exists, the result is
UNAVAILABLE, not a fabricated operating limit. T38 will create and govern
actual submission, independent review, approval, supersession and withdrawal
and its configurable authority assignments. This allocation does not pre-approve
T38 implementation or remove its own acceptance gate.

**T36 selection and implementation registration.** T36 (G4) is **SELECTED for
implementation** under the conditional exact file ledger immediately above,
which is adopted as the initial file allowlist for this registered class;

T33, T08 and T09 are completed. T15 already exercises trusted lineage

#### Source baseline and admitted scope

T08 can commission and rotate a point binding and its direct mapping.
Its Topology ownership contract admits active FACILITY and EQUIPMENT only.
Reuse those exact asset kinds. HidraWEB can pass an explicitly linked,
authorized equipment ID from the T35 dossier or an authorized facility ID.
Pipeline, section and system IDs do not serve as commissioning assets.
Cross-asset observation aggregation, new asset kinds, new writes and
changes to T08/T09 routes are outside this task.

T09 exact and history reads start from a known point and authorize its
current binding. History sorts by trust publication time. Those operations
cannot discover commissioned points by asset or prove that a historical row
belongs to that asset when measured. A trusted row already pins raw,
assessment, binding, quantity, source timestamp and publication time.
The raw ingest receipt pins the source, unit and mapping. Use those
stored references to establish each row's exact historical lineage.

#### Public read contract

Root `/api/v1/telemetry/assets/{assetType}/{assetId}/points`.
All operations are ordinary authenticated GETs, with explicit
`companyPartyId`, stable operation IDs, typed OpenAPI and private no-store.

| Relative route | Operation ID | Contract |
|---|---|---|
| Collection root | `listAssetScopedTelemetryPoints` | List eligible commissioned points at one `at` instant (defaults to server time, future instants rejected). Return point, source, available unit and exact applicable binding ID/window. Sort by point ID. Use limit 1–50, default 20, and an optional after-point cursor. Derive any next cursor only after authorization and eligibility filtering. An authorized asset with no visible commissioned points returns an empty list. |
| `/{pointId}/trusted-readings/latest` | `readLatestAssetScopedTrustedObservation` | Resolve the unique current binding, exact asset membership and current point/source grant. Select the newest trusted publication by observation timestamp and trusted ID within that binding. Older publications from prior bindings are excluded. Report FRESH, STALE or UNAVAILABLE. A stale value carries its original provenance. Missing or incompatible evidence returns UNAVAILABLE with no observation payload. Do not substitute an older sample when the newest candidate for that binding has incompatible lineage. |
| `/{pointId}/trusted-readings/history` | `listAssetScopedTrustedObservationHistory` | Require explicit UTC `from` and `until` over a half-open observation-time window, at most 31 days and ending no later than server time. Authorize the point's asset membership within the window and each historical source. Match each candidate to its recorded binding at measurement time. Return only qualifying rows, by observation time descending then trusted ID descending. Limit 1–50, default 20, with an optional validated observation-time and trusted-ID cursor scoped to the same filter. Empty authorized history returns an empty list. |

Use one captured server instant per request. Latest and history take the
required UI freshness threshold `maxAgeSeconds` in 1–604800. Report the
evaluation instant, threshold and age from the source timestamp. Age at or
below the threshold is FRESH, age above it is STALE. This threshold expresses
client display policy and leaves stored T09 quality and trust unchanged.
A future-dated observation never becomes FRESH. Use FRESHNESS_UNAVAILABLE
for a history entry whose age cannot be established. No unit conversion
or inferred value. Expose the typed stored value, available unit identity,
source ID, source and receipt times, assessment ID/status, quality code,
trust level, trust-publication time, raw and trusted IDs, and recorded
binding ID/effective interval. Respect Telemetry's unit-exempt signal shapes.

#### Authorization and consistency

Resolve exact current Topology ownership and current T33 permission before
enumeration. Apply the existing Telemetry TRUSTED_READ paired company and
exact source/point policy to discovery and observations. Neither regional
access nor a Telemetry grant alone suffices. A historical binding is data
lineage. It never confers present authority. For history and historical
discovery, check current authority over the requested owner and applicable
historical source/point; a current binding to another asset confers no
authority over the old one. For latest, require exact currently commissioned
membership. Use the T33/T35 status conventions: 401 unauthenticated, 403
for ordinary route denial, uniform protected 404 for absent/foreign/denied
exact scope or wrong asset/point, and 400 for invalid query syntax. Suppress
unauthorized list rows before deriving the slice or cursor. Do not emit
unfiltered counts or existence hints.

At the observation timestamp, require one matching binding under the
half-open validity rule and an exact match among the trusted row, assessment,
raw observation, ingest receipt, pinned direct mapping, source/point and unit.
Validate the recorded historical unit and mapping against the evidence;
never substitute a successor's unit, source or binding. Exclude ambiguous,
unpublished, failed or incompatible lineage. Use bounded parameterized
owner reads and the established owner-scope transaction/locking patterns.
Recheck applicable exact owner/authority and scope after assembly before
disclosure, with no durable or token-cached scope decisions.

#### Single T37 development-software acceptance gate

One passing HidraAPI CI Full Verification Gate on the final reconciled
implementation SHA is sufficient. Its signed HTTP journey must prove:

1. An authorized regional reader discovers a commissioned point from a
   permitted asset, sees a fresh latest and ordered history, and receives
   exact source, unit, timestamp, quality, trust and binding lineage.
2. A genuine T08 binding successor moves the point to a second eligible
   asset. Include pre-boundary, exact-boundary and post-boundary observations.
   Latest follows only the current binding. Historical reads and discovery
   use the applicable historical binding and never mix the assets. Use
   an authorized historical read after the existing JVM restart to prove
   that provenance remains independently retrievable.
3. A stale trusted observation is explicitly stale. A commissioned point
   without publication is unavailable for latest and has empty history.
   Prove wrong-unit and wrong-binding evidence through the existing native
   admission guards and verify that no raw, failed or incompatible reading
   appears in any T37 response. Show that a post-filter page can still
   return a later authorized row and exposes no hidden counts or cursor.
4. Cover signed readers in different regional scopes, a foreign company,
   regional-only and Telemetry-only grants, wrong asset/point, and current
   revocation on a previously issued token. Check protected response parity,
   route gating, and both architecture scanners.

The same gate includes full registered regression, all PostgreSQL shards,
inventory, generated OpenAPI backward compatibility and strict equality,
and strict physical dictionary equality. Retain the same-run combined
artifact and link the gate. This closes the software task without a separate

#### T38 execution contract

- Add an exact Topology owner resource under
  `/api/v1/topology/operating-constraints/pipelines/{pipelineId}/restriction-requests`,
  with POST submission, GET exact request, POST `/{requestId}/publication`
  and GET `/{requestId}/evidence`. Use explicit company context and nullable
  section, an exact condition and effective period, and separate DTOs
  for initial restriction, replacement and withdrawal. Reuse existing T36
  effective/historical GETs and Workflow review/assignment routes. Treat
  client receipt IDs, expected stream version and request IDs as references
  and concurrency controls. Derive actor, source digest, source revision,
  decision time and audit linkage from owner evidence. Source is the exact
  admitted T07 network publication pin. Preserve T07 protected reads.
- Check T33 canonical pipeline/section and current Organization responsibility
  plus distinct configurable Identity operations for submit, review, publish,
  and evidence read. Authorize before exposing lookup, CAS or conflict data.
  Workflow start requires the immutable candidate's authenticated submitter
  and live submit authority. REVIEW requires an independently assigned
  eligible human, current exact review authority and T30 configuration
  and transition checks. For pressure targets, apply the owner check in
  previews and execution, including the generic Workflow route. Exact
  readback uses current authority and independent evidence permission
  before returning Audit or decision details. Return non-disclosing 404
  for absent/denied owner targets, 400 for invalid input and 409 for an
  authorized stale, invalid lifecycle or replay conflict.
- Submit in one owner transaction to persist request idempotency, expected
  stream version, and immutable candidate IDs. Review uses the existing
  atomic T30 decision transaction. A committed review alone changes no
  effective pressure. Owner publication independently requires exact
  final APPROVE evidence bound to candidate and locator, current reviewer
  eligibility and publisher authority. Recheck relevant authority and source
  at the write boundary. Use a separate protected T07 preflight outside
  the owner write transaction and validate/lock the exact immutable source
  and current structural bindings at publication. Preserve the separate
  transaction boundaries. A failed publication leaves the review intact
  and leaves all owner publication and Audit writes rolled back.
- Initial publication consumes one REVISION approval. Withdrawal consumes
  one WITHDRAW approval against the exact current revision. Supersession
  preserves the two existing immutable candidate and Workflow identities,
  REVISION for the successor and SUPERSEDE for the retirement. T36's current
  target lookup requires an already published successor for SUPERSEDE.
  Admit instead the same request's immutable successor candidate with
  identical scope, source, predecessor and boundary; retain the existing
  committed successor check for historical or legacy readback. Verify both
  final decisions, then insert the successor first and termination second,
  with both distinct Audit receipts and stream advancement in one transaction.
  Retain T36's existing database admission and no-resurrection rules.
- Serialize publication on the exact company/system/pipeline/section/condition
  stream, compare the expected version and applicable prior revision, reject
  conflicting intervals or a second termination, and consume each decision
  once. Authorize retries before receipt disclosure. Same key and canonical
  payload replays the original receipt, and a changed payload or stale
  version conflicts without a partial write. Use the existing protected
  publication credential via an exact caller fence, forward-only owner
  SQL functions with fixed search path, exact execution grants and typed
  parameters. Keep ordinary runtime direct writes and destructive updates
  to immutable evidence denied. Do not weaken existing T36 triggers or
  retrofit already accepted history.

has 491 paths, 536 operations and 586 schemas. The raw JSON SHA-256 sealed

T36 qualified restrictions, T37 asset observations and T38 decisions.
The separate T33/T34 regional suite already tests authorization before
counts, paging and geometry. T39 links the owner routes through the
same selected feature and related asset in the signed qualification
suite. No new runtime endpoint, permission, policy, DTO, migration or
engine is required by the admitted scope.

Reuse the existing signed LOCAL authentication and fresh PostgreSQL
fixture. Add a browser-replayable synthetic region to the same test
fixture with a map-discoverable GZ2 pipeline/section, a genuinely linked
equipment/facility target for the commissioned point, a disjoint
same-company region and a foreign company. Select an authorized map or
search feature, derive its pipeline and linked target from owner
responses, and use those returned identifiers for dossier, constraint
and Telemetry calls. The contract must identify the exact navigation
fields and any lookup hop. Fixture identifiers can assert correctness
but must not bypass the navigation.
Specifically, use the authorized `pipelines` feature's
`properties.entityId` as the dossier and pipeline-constraint path ID,
select the section by `items[].id` from the dossier sections response,
and use an authorized equipment item's `facilityId` for the existing
`FACILITY` Telemetry discovery route. Use the returned `pointId` for
latest/history and the returned T38 `requestId` for publication and
evidence. Verify the chosen section is the equipment association where
the fixture provides one.

#### T39 single backend acceptance gate

One successful **Full Verification Gate** for the T39 implementation SHA
must include the fresh signed PostgreSQL journey, generated runtime
OpenAPI and existing strict API/dictionary checks. The reviewed handoff
must resolve its documented routes and operationIds against that contract.
The signed suite must check these cases in the same run:

1. A regional user can discover the intended pipeline/section, including
   authorized feature/GeoJSON output and scoped paging or counts. A second
   regional user sees their own resources. Foreign or unentitled users
   cannot discover protected identifiers, geometry or totals from the
   same collection/detail routes. Recheck discoverability and a protected
   detail with an already-issued token after revocation.
2. The discovered identifiers resolve the same pipeline dossier, source
   or published baseline receipt and linked observation target. Preserve
   design-pressure meaning, approved effective pressure with basis and
   units, and an explicit unavailable constraint without falling back to
   design pressure. Distinguish fresh, stale and unavailable observations
   from the approved limit. Verify trusted reading source, binding revision,
   observation time and historical scope, reusing the existing T37 cases.
3. Verify the admitted Workflow review and Topology publication are
   distinct. Authorized readback carries the exact candidate/decision,
   action and Audit event reference and the correct effective owner
   outcome. Wrong regional/company scope and revoked authority receive
   the route's opaque denial. Preserve T38's replacement, withdrawal,
   one-winner race, rollback and post-restart assertions.
4. The successful shard-1 raw report contains the asserted handoff
   receipt with enough synthetic fixture locators, roles and timestamps
   to replay the path. The same full evidence bundle supplies the exact
   runtime OpenAPI and its digest; use its SHA/run/attempt, gate receipt
   and artifact manifest to resolve provenance without embedding the
   future implementation commit SHA in its own source. The same fixture
   is reusable locally for HidraWEB via the documented bounded harness.
   Report artifacts must exclude tokens, passwords, signing material and
   database credentials.

The full-gate bundle, checked-in runbook and test fixture constitute all
T39 backend acceptance evidence. No separate manual API run, secondary
backend workflow, SITE or operational sign-off is required. Independent
HidraWEB browser acceptance on the pinned consumer/backend SHAs remains
the product integration gate under HidraWEB governance. T39 selects no
HidraWEB implementation, deployment, live OT or numerical solver work.
